title: Add TIFF compression and JPEG quality options to Save Plot as Image
description:
## Summary

Plots saved as TIFF from the Plots pane were always uncompressed, and JPEGs were always saved at quality 100. With the fixed plot size and export resolution options from #18895, a 7 x 5 in plot at 600 DPI was a 36 MB TIFF.

- **Save Plot as Image** now has a **Compression** menu for TIFFs (LZW by default, or ZIP, each with or without a predictor where R offers them) and a **Quality** menu for JPEGs (100, the previous behaviour, by default). Each is shown for its format only, and both are remembered in `export_plot_options` alongside the format and resolution.
- The compressions are listed by the session from the running R's `tiff()` formals (`.rs.graphics.tiffCompressionTypes()`), restricted to the lossless ones ragg's `agg_tiff()` also maps. `rle` is left out because it fails for colour images, `jpeg` because it is lossy at a fixed quality, and the recent `lerc` / `lzma` / `zstd` / `webp` because libtiff and viewers may not support them and ragg doesn't know them.
- The values go to `grDevices::tiff(compression = )` / `jpeg(quality = )` and to `ragg::agg_tiff()` / `agg_jpeg()`, so no new native dependency is needed. The compression name is validated before it is interpolated into R code.
- `.rs.api.savePlotAsImage()` gains optional `compression` and `quality` arguments.

### Quartz (macOS)

R's Quartz devices ignore both arguments (`tiff()` warns, `jpeg()` silently drops the quality) and write through ImageIO with no properties. Measured on macOS 14, 15 and 26: ImageIO writes TIFFs uncompressed by default, honours compression 5 (LZW) and 8 (ZIP) through `kCGImagePropertyTIFFDictionary`, and Quartz's `jpeg()` always writes at ImageIO's default quality, whatever `quality` says.

So the ImageIO rewrite that already records the resolution (now `RGraphicsQuartzImage.cpp`, replacing `RGraphicsImageResolution.cpp`) also compresses TIFFs, and a JPEG is drawn as a PNG and encoded through ImageIO at the chosen quality (re-encoding Quartz's own JPEG would lose more). On macOS, "100" therefore now genuinely means 100, which is larger than the default-quality file Quartz used to write. ImageIO has no predictor option, so the Quartz list offers None, LZW and ZIP.

### Measurements

The same 7 x 5 in plot (R-devel on Windows; `windows` is the default device there, `cairo` is Linux's):

| Output | 300 DPI | 600 DPI |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TIFF, none | 9.01 MB | 36.05 MB |
| TIFF, LZW (`windows`) | 0.10 MB | 0.28 MB |
| TIFF, LZW (`cairo`) | 0.29 MB | 0.73 MB |
| TIFF, ZIP (`cairo`) | 0.29 MB | 0.70 MB |
| JPEG, quality 100 | 0.51 MB | 1.35 MB |
| JPEG, quality 95 | 0.31 MB | 0.82 MB |

## Testing

- R (`test-graphics.R`): every compression the session offers writes the matching TIFF compression tag (259); the default is LZW and under half the size of an uncompressed save; an invalid compression name is an error; a JPEG at quality 50 is smaller than at 100 and still records its resolution.
- e2e (`plots_pane.test.ts`): the Compression and Quality menus appear for their formats only, with LZW and 100 selected; a TIFF saved through the dialog carries compression tag 5.
- The existing `plots_pane.test.ts` and `fixed_plot_size.test.ts` specs pass on Windows (desktop-dev).
- Not covered: the macOS code path (ImageIO's behaviour was measured on GitHub runners with a stand-alone program, but this build was not run on a Mac); the Viewer pane's export, which is an Electron screenshot and cannot produce TIFF.

Addresses #19114.

title: Skip empty RETICULATE_PYTHON test on Windows
description:
On Windows, setting an environment variable to an empty string removes it. `withr::local_envvar(c(RETICULATE_PYTHON = ""))` therefore leaves `RETICULATE_PYTHON` unset, and the "startup preserves an explicitly empty Python configuration" test can't create the state it checks. With reticulate installed, `.rs.inferReticulatePython(discover = FALSE)` returns `NULL` and the test fails. Without reticulate it returns the final `""`, so the test passed only by coincidence.

The test now skips on Windows (`skip_on_os("windows")`).

Verified on Windows x64 with `rstudio-tests.bat --scope r --filter reticulate`: the test reports `SKIP ... Reason: On Windows`, and the run ends `[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 9 | PASS 16 ]`.

Fixes #19110.

title: Configure worktree build dirs with Ninja
description:
`scripts/bootstrap-worktree.sh --with-build-dir` now passes `-G Ninja` when configuring the worktree's `build/`. Without `-G`, CMake used the Makefiles generator, so the bare `cmake --build` run by `npm run rserver-dev` compiled serially.

Ninja is already a required dependency in `install-dependencies-osx` and the Linux install scripts.

Verified by bootstrapping a fresh worktree: its `CMakeCache.txt` has `CMAKE_GENERATOR:INTERNAL=Ninja`.

Fixes #19144.

title: tidy up NEWS.md for 2026.11
description:
Tidies up NEWS.md for 2026.11:

- Removes the `RSTUDIO_WHICH_R` entry (from #19116) and a stray empty bullet.
- Links the startup performance entry to its issue (#19142) instead of PR #19030.
- Adds missing trailing periods to four entries under "Fixed".

title: Stop wrapping Tab focus inside modal dialogs
description:
Fixes #19134.

Modal dialogs no longer wrap Tab focus. As with a native modal `<dialog>`, Tab past the last control or Shift+Tab past the first is left to the browser, which moves focus to its own controls (or to the host page when RStudio is embedded, e.g. in Posit Cloud). Focus can't reach anything behind the dialog, because `ModalDialogTracker` makes it inert. The issue covers why we're dropping the wrap.

- `ModalDialogBase` no longer handles Tab. `focusFirstControl()` finds the first focusable control when called, instead of reading a marker class; it still sets the default initial focus. `deferRefreshFocusableElements()` becomes `deferFocusInitialControl()`, used by `Wizard`.
- `FocusHelper` keeps only its static `setFocusDeferred` helpers. The first/last marker classes and their upkeep in `DialogTabLayoutPanel`, `PreferencesDialogBase` and `PackageActionConfirmationDialog` are removed.
- Non-modal popups are attached to `<body>`, outside the containers `ModalDialogTracker` made inert, so a popup already showing when a modal opened was reachable. When the first modal opens, the tracker now also makes the other elements already attached to `<body>` inert, and restores them when the last modal closes. Popups opened afterwards, such as menus and suggestion lists opened from the dialog, stay usable.

### Tests

The Global Options wrap tests are replaced. Headless browsers have no controls of their own to tab to, so Tab off the end of the page cycles back into it, and the old wrap assertions would pass with or without the trap. The new tests check that:

- the Tab and Shift+Tab keydowns off either end aren't prevented
- focus stays in the dialog or leaves the page
- a focusable element attached to `<body>` before the dialog opens can't be reached, and is no longer inert after the dialog closes

The new tests failed before the change and pass after it (`test:server-dev`). `tests/preferences`, `import_dataset` and `packages_pane` also pass. I also checked by hand that the Install Packages suggestion list works over the dialog and that the New Project wizard sets initial focus on each page.

Not yet verified on RStudio Desktop or Posit Cloud.

### Companion

rstudio/rstudio-pro#13233 updates the Workbench e2e page objects that located dialog controls through the removed marker classes.

title: cache reticulate's error hint when python is initialized
description:
## Summary

The R session could hang (Linux) or crash (macOS) when the Environment pane listed Python objects while reticulate was formatting the session's first Python error. The server e2e suite hit it as a hang in `run_chunks_above_console_python.test.ts` (run 38772279901 on #19115).

reticulate 1.29 to 1.47 computes the hint it appends to Python error messages ("Run `reticulate::py_last_error()` for details") in a function-local static's initializer, by calling R. RStudio answers RPCs from `R_ProcessEvents()` while that R code runs. When the REPL starts, the client switches the Environment pane to Python and requests `get_environment_state`. Listing `__main__` calls `py_is_callable()` on the `r` object, whose attribute lookup calls into R and raises. That formats a second error, which re-enters the initializer: libstdc++ waits on the init guard forever, and libc++ aborts. The upstream fix is rstudio/reticulate#1936 (issue rstudio/reticulate#1935).

- `.rs.reticulate.onPythonInitialized()` now formats one Python exception through reticulate before the client is told Python is available, so reticulate computes and caches the hint before any Environment pane request can race it. Since it calls a reticulate internal, it is guarded with `exists()`, and the `.rs.reticulate.cacheErrorHint()` wrapper logs any error from `.rs.reticulate.cacheErrorHintImpl()` instead of letting it fail Python initialization. With a fixed reticulate it just caches the hint early.
- The server e2e fixture now dismisses the "previous R session was abnormally terminated" notice after `PW_RSTUDIO_SERVER_RECOVER_CMD` replaces a stuck session. In that run, recovery worked, but the notice blocked the Files tab click until the 120 s fixture timeout, so the retry failed too.

## Testing

- `test-reticulate.R`: after Python is initialized, formatting a Python error does not call `.py_last_error_hint()`. Fails against main's R sources (the hint is computed on that first error) and passes with this change. A second test stubs the implementation to throw and checks that the wrapper logs the error and returns `FALSE`. The rest of the file passes.
- `test:server-dev` (macOS): `run_chunks_above_console_python.test.ts` passes. A throwaway spec (not committed) killed the rsession with SIGKILL, reloaded, and the new locator found and dismissed the real notice.
- Not covered: the full recovery path (it needs a session that is actually stuck), and Linux, where the original hang happened.

Fixes #19130.

title: fall back to mode bits when a claim directory acl write is denied
description:
### Intent

Since 2026.10.0 (#18747), every session for a project whose `.Rproj.user` lives on a default ntfs-3g mount dies at startup: creating the lock-claim directory copies the parent's POSIX ACL onto it, `acl_set_fd` fails with `EPERM`, the source-database lock reports the error, and session initialization suicides.

Fixes #19118. Targets `rel-blue-mistflower` so the fix ships with the next 2026.10 patch build; main picks it up through the usual release-branch merge. Supersedes #19123, which targeted main.

### Approach

ntfs-3g mounted without `uid=` or `permissions` lets a user create a directory but reports it as owned by root, so the kernel rejects the ACL write with `EPERM` while still accepting `fchmod`. `applyTranslatedPosixAcl` only tolerated `ENOTSUP`/`EOPNOTSUPP`; it now also takes the existing mode-bit fallback when `acl_set_fd` fails with `EPERM` on a directory that reports an owner other than the creating process. The Darwin branch gets the same check. Any other failure, including `EPERM` on a directory the process owns, still fails the acquisition.

Reproduced in a privileged `ubuntu:22.04` container with a loop-mounted NTFS image: a non-root user's `mkdir` succeeds, the child stats as `uid=0`, `acl_set_fd` returns `EPERM`, `fchmod` succeeds. Mounts with `uid=<user>` or `-o permissions` do not hit this.

### NEWS

The release branch has no `NEWS.md`, so the entry starts `version/news/os/NEWS-2026.10.1-blue-mistflower.md`.

### Automated Tests

Three gtests in `FileLockTests.cpp`, driven by new `setForceClaimDirectoryAclFailureForTesting(errno)` and `setForceClaimDirectoryForeignOwnerForTesting(bool)` hooks: `EPERM` on a foreign-owned directory falls back to the parent's mode bits; `EPERM` on a self-owned directory, and `EACCES`/`EIO` on a foreign-owned one, still fail. The first test fails without the fix.

### QA Notes

On Linux: mount an NTFS image with `ntfs-3g img /mnt/ntfs` (no options) as root, put a project under it, open it as a normal user. Before this change the session fails to start with `acl_set_fd ... Operation not permitted` in the rsession log.

### Documentation

None.

title: Document testing an unpublished GWT SDK
description:
Adds a "Testing with RStudio" section to `src/gwt/tools/build-gwt-README.md` for building RStudio against a locally built GWT fork SDK before it is published.

- `ant -Dgwt.sdk=<fork>/build/staging/gwt-<version> draft` overrides the SDK location from `src/gwt/build.xml`. The other libraries still come from the installed `gwtproject`.
- `rserver-dev` doesn't forward `ant` arguments, so the override is passed through `ANT_ARGS`, with `--restart` so a running instance doesn't keep the old SDK.
- The step that copies the SDK over `dependencies/common/gwtproject/gwt/gwt-rstudio` moves to Publishing, where packaging the tarball still needs it. For testing, the override replaces it. A copy would change the SDK for every worktree that falls back to the primary checkout's `dependencies/`, and `install-gwt` won't restore the original while its marker file exists.
- `RSTUDIO` is now assigned explicitly in both sections' commands.

Verified that `ant -Dgwt.sdk=/nonexistent/gwt-sdk javac` and `ANT_ARGS="-Dgwt.sdk=/nonexistent/gwt-sdk" ant javac` both fail with `/nonexistent/gwt-sdk does not exist`, confirming each route reaches the build.

title: Accept an R home directory in RSTUDIO_WHICH_R
description:
## Summary

RStudio Desktop reads `RSTUDIO_WHICH_R` as the path of the R executable (`bin\x64\Rterm.exe` on Windows), so a home directory such as `C:\R\R-4.5.3` landed in the "choose R" dialog, or failed validation.

The variable now also accepts an R home directory, which resolves to the executable it holds: `bin/x64/Rterm.exe`, then `bin/i386/Rterm.exe`, on Windows, and `bin/R` elsewhere. Any other value (an executable, a directory holding no R, a path that doesn't exist) is used as given, so validation still reports it. The resolver is applied everywhere the variable is read: the Windows startup prompt, the early background detection, and both scans.

## Testing

- Unit (`detect-r.test.ts`): a home directory resolves to its executable, an executable and a missing path are left alone, a directory with no R is left alone, and the 32-bit executable is the Windows fallback.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` are clean.
- Manually on Windows: the Playwright desktop-dev suite launched with `RSTUDIO_WHICH_R=C:\R\R-4.6.1` starts R 4.6.1 (it previously needed `...\bin\x64\R.exe`).

title: resolve @rpath dependencies in verify-library-paths.sh
description:
### Intent

Since #19068, `verify-library-paths.sh` fails the package build for any dependency that isn't part of macOS or under `@executable_path/../Frameworks/`, and that now includes `@rpath/...` dependencies. `license-manager` (Workbench Desktop) loads TurboActivate and TurboFloat as `@rpath/libTurboActivate.dylib` and `@rpath/libTurboFloat.dylib`, with an rpath of `@executable_path/../Frameworks` (`Frameworks/arm64` for the arm64 copy). So the Workbench macOS package build fails this check:

```
error: '.../bin/license-manager' loads '@rpath/libTurboActivate.dylib', which is not part of macOS
```

Follow-up to rstudio/rstudio-pro#13101.

### Approach

Resolve each `@rpath/<lib>` dependency against the file's own `LC_RPATH` entries. Only rpaths relative to `@executable_path` count: an absolute rpath left behind by the build (e.g. the CMake build tree) may resolve on the build machine but won't on a user's. If no rpath leads to the library inside the bundle, the check fails as before.

Keeping this check strict, instead of special-casing libraries, is also what protects us if we ever switch OpenSSL (or anything else) back to shared linking without bundling it: the build fails here with a clear message rather than at launch on a user's machine.

### Automated Tests

None in-tree; the script has no test harness. Tested by hand against small bundles built with a `@rpath` dylib:

| rpath | library location | result |
|---|---|---|
| `@executable_path/../Frameworks` | `Frameworks/` | pass |
| `@executable_path/../Frameworks` | missing | error |
| `@executable_path/../Frameworks/arm64` | `Frameworks/arm64/` | pass |
| `@executable_path/../Frameworks/arm64` | `Frameworks/` only | error |
| `@executable_path` | `bin/` | pass |
| absolute path outside the bundle | `Frameworks/` and that path | error |

Also ran it on a `license-manager` binary given the package-build rpath, with the Turbo libraries in `Frameworks/`: the TurboActivate/TurboFloat errors are gone.

### QA Notes

Build-only change; nothing to verify in the product.

### Documentation

None needed.

### Checklist

- [ ] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` (n/a: build tooling, unreleased)
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility) (n/a)

title: Point agents and install scripts to the GWT fork README
description:
Nothing in the repo linked to `src/gwt/tools/build-gwt-README.md`, so people and agents updating `GWT_VERSION` had no pointer to the build and publish steps.

- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `src/gwt/CLAUDE.md`: note that RStudio builds against a GWT fork, and link to the README.
- `dependencies/common/install-gwt` and `dependencies/windows/install-dependencies.cmd`: add a comment above `GWT_VERSION` pointing to the README. In `install-gwt` this replaces the comment "The version of Boost to be downloaded and built", which was a copy-paste error.

title: Replace sync-gwt with GWT build and publish docs
description:
Removes `src/gwt/tools/sync-gwt` and rewrites `src/gwt/tools/build-gwt-README.md` to document how the GWT SDK is built from the rstudio/gwt fork and published to the `rstudio-buildtools` S3 bucket.

`sync-gwt` wasn't called from anywhere. It cloned the repos, merged upstream `main` into a local `main` (release branches merge upstream tags, not `main`), and printed the build/publish runbook. The README now contains that runbook, with these fixes:

- The packaging step was `tar czf gwt.tar.gz` with no input files, which fails. It is now `tar czf ../gwt.tar.gz *`, which produces the same layout as the current `gwt-2.13.1-montauk-daisy.tar.gz`.
- Notes that the build needs a gwtproject/tools checkout at `../tools` or `GWT_TOOLS`.
- Removes the RStudio 1.3 content (checked-in SDK, nonexistent `build-gwt` script).
- Adds a naming convention for repeat builds within a release (`2.13.1-montauk-daisy`, then `-1`, `-2`, ...). Names are never reused, and each build is tagged with its name in rstudio/gwt to record which commit it came from.
- Lists all the places to bump the version, including `dependencies/metadata/gwt.txt`.

Also updates the GWT version in `dependencies/metadata/gwt.txt` from 2.12.2 to 2.13.1 to match `install-gwt` (`2.13.1-montauk-daisy`).

title: Drop hardcoded WCAG level and version from a11y test titles
description:
The three accessibility state tests were titled "… has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations". Since #19120, `PW_A11Y_LEVEL` and `PW_A11Y_WCAG_VERSION` choose the rule set, so an AAA or 2.1 run reported under an "AA"/"2.2" title. They are now "… has no accessibility violations".

The rule set used, e.g. `WCAG 2.2 AAA`, is still recorded in each state's `axe-results.json` and on the run's Summary page.

title: fall back to mode bits when a claim directory acl write is denied
description:
### Intent

Since 2026.10.0 (#18747), every session for a project whose `.Rproj.user` lives on a default ntfs-3g mount dies at startup: creating the lock-claim directory copies the parent's POSIX ACL onto it, `acl_set_fd` fails with `EPERM`, the source-database lock reports the error, and session initialization suicides.

Fixes #19118.

### Approach

ntfs-3g mounted without `uid=` or `permissions` lets a user create a directory but reports it as owned by root, so the kernel rejects the ACL write with `EPERM` while still accepting `fchmod`. `applyTranslatedPosixAcl` only tolerated `ENOTSUP`/`EOPNOTSUPP`; it now treats `EPERM` and `EACCES` from `acl_set_fd` the same way and takes the existing mode-bit fallback. The Darwin branch gets the same classification. Any other errno still fails the acquisition.

Reproduced in a privileged `ubuntu:22.04` container with a loop-mounted NTFS image: a non-root user's `mkdir` succeeds, the child stats as `uid=0`, `acl_set_fd` returns `EPERM`, `fchmod` succeeds. Mounts with `uid=<user>` or `-o permissions` do not hit this.

### Automated Tests

Two gtests in `FileLockTests.cpp`, driven by a new `setForceClaimDirectoryAclFailureForTesting(errno)` hook that fails the ACL write with a chosen errno: `EPERM` now yields a claim directory with the parent's mode bits and a successful acquire, while `EIO` still fails. The first test fails without the fix.

### QA Notes

On Linux: mount an NTFS image with `ntfs-3g img /mnt/ntfs` (no options) as root, put a project under it, open it as a normal user. Before this change the session fails to start with `acl_set_fd ... Operation not permitted` in the rsession log.

### Documentation

None.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: Make a11y scan WCAG level and version configurable
description:
Adds two settings to the accessibility (axe-core) scans: the WCAG conformance level and the WCAG version. The defaults, AA and 2.2, select the same axe tags as before.

| Setting | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PW_A11Y_LEVEL` | `A`, `AA`, `AAA` | `AA` |
| `PW_A11Y_WCAG_VERSION` | `2.1`, `2.2` | `2.2` |

A level includes the levels below it, and a version includes earlier versions:
- `A` drops the AA rules, including `target-size`.
- `AAA` adds axe's three `wcag2aaa` rules (`color-contrast-enhanced`, `identical-links-same-purpose`, `meta-refresh-no-exceptions`). axe has no 2.1 or 2.2 AAA rules.
- `2.1` drops `wcag22aa` (`target-size`).

With `PW_A11Y_EXPERIMENTAL`, experimental results are now filtered to the selected tags rather than the fixed A/AA set. Each state's `axe-results.json` and the run's Summary page record the rule set, e.g. `WCAG 2.1 AAA`. An unrecognized value stops the run when the config loads.

**Workflows:** the accessibility workflow has `level` and `wcag_version` choice inputs, which it passes to new `a11y_level` / `a11y_wcag_version` inputs on the Server workflow.

```bash
gh workflow run os-test-e2e-rstudio-a11y-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml -f level=AAA -f wcag_version=2.1
PW_A11Y=1 PW_A11Y_LEVEL=AAA PW_A11Y_WCAG_VERSION=2.1 npx playwright test --project=server
```

`playwright.config.ts`'s allow-list env parser (`resolveEnvMode`) moves to `utils/env.ts` as `envChoice` so the a11y utilities can share it.

**Testing:** `tests/a11y/scan-config.test.ts` now covers level A, level AAA and WCAG 2.1 against its synthetic page, using a new 4.54:1 contrast element that fails only AAA. `tests/harness/env-flag.test.ts` covers `envChoice` defaults, accepted values and rejection. Both pass locally, as does `tsc --noEmit`. The workflow inputs have not been run on CI yet.

title: Document git worktree setup in CLAUDE.md
description: Adds a short "Git Worktrees" section to `.claude/CLAUDE.md` so agents working in a worktree (e.g. for code review) know to run `scripts/bootstrap-worktree.sh --with-build-dir` once, rely on the primary checkout's `dependencies/`, and not copy or symlink the primary checkout's `build/`.

title: Fix state leaks and wait races in a11y Packages and untitled-script scans
description:
Follow-up to #19111, addressing review findings on two of its accessibility states. Test-only change.

**`packages-pane.test.ts`**

The selected pane tab is client state that outlives the session, so a Packages selection left on the server makes later states open on Packages.

- Files is restored in a `finally`, so a failed stats check or scan no longer skips the restore.
- After activating Packages, the test waits for the tab-state save carrying it. Activation selects the tab synchronously, so any save after it carries Packages; seeing it guarantees that switching back produces a save to wait for.
- The wait for the Files save starts before `activateFiles`, so a save that fires during the toolbar wait is not missed.
- If the Packages save was not seen within 15 s (the client sends pending changes every 5 s), the test logs a warning and restores Files anyway rather than throwing before the restore.

The test now takes about 10.6 s locally instead of 2.5 s, since it always waits for both saves.

**`untitled-r-script.test.ts`**

The test records the active document's id before `newSourceDoc` and waits for a different untitled document. Session teardown can leave an untitled tab behind, which previously satisfied the wait before the new document existed.

**Testing**

`PW_A11Y=1 npm run test:server-dev` locally: each state test gets through its waits and fails only on the existing axe violations, and the untitled-script state opened on Files after the Packages state. Running the Packages test alone, both with a failure injected into the scan and with the Packages save deliberately missed, the logged requests show Files saved (`TabSet2: 0`) after Packages (`TabSet2: 2`).

title: add a fixed plot size option to the plots pane
description:
## Summary

Plots can now be drawn at a fixed size instead of the size of the Plots pane, so a figure can be iterated on in the IDE the way it will look in the final output, with no `png()` / external viewer loop.

- **UI**: a new size menu on the Plots pane toolbar (it shows "Fit to Pane" or the current size, e.g. "7 x 5 in"), with the same two items in the Plots menu and the Command Palette: **Fit to Pane** and **Fixed Size...**. The dialog takes a width and height in inches, centimeters, or pixels (96 DPI). Switching units converts the values, and sizes outside 1-30 in are rejected.
- **Display**: resizing the pane no longer redraws the plot. The pane shows it at its true size when it fits, and scales it down (keeping its aspect ratio) and centers it when it doesn't, with a faint outline marking the plot's edges. The Zoom window scales the plot to the window and renders it at a higher pixel ratio so that it stays sharp.
- **Export**: Save as Image / PDF and Copy to Clipboard default to the fixed size, since they already default to the plot's size. A fixed size too large to preview is kept rather than clamped to the screen (the preview is hidden, as it already was for sizes beyond it).
- **Interaction**: `locator()` and manipulator clicks are mapped from the scaled, centered image back to the plot's coordinates.

### Exporting at a precise physical size

For a plot pasted into a Word document (or similar) to come out at a precise size, the image file has to carry its resolution: that's how those applications decide an inserted bitmap's physical size.

- **Save as Image resolution**: for plots, the "Use device pixel ratio" checkbox becomes a **Resolution** choice: Screen (the display's, the old default), 96, 150, 300, or 600 DPI. It is disabled for vector formats. The width and height stay in pixels at 96 DPI (what the preview shows), so a higher resolution adds detail without changing the layout. The text next to it shows the result, e.g. "4 x 3 in, 1200 x 900 pixels". The Viewer's export, a screenshot of the page, keeps the checkbox.
- **macOS resolution metadata**: R's `quartz()` bitmap devices, the default on macOS, don't record the resolution in the files they write. This is [R PR#19076](https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19076), which has a patch acknowledged by R-core but not yet committed. PNGs have no `pHYs`, JPEGs a 72:72 aspect ratio, TIFFs no resolution tags, and BMPs 0 ppm, so Word inserted them at the wrong size. That affected Copy to Clipboard too, since AppKit sizes the copied image from the same file. After saving a bitmap, RStudio now reads its resolution back and, if it's missing or wrong, rewrites the file through ImageIO with the DPI (as the upstream patch does). It also marks the JFIF density as dots per inch, since ImageIO always writes the aspect-ratio form. This is a no-op for Cairo and ragg output, and for Quartz once R records the resolution itself.
- Fixed an unrelated bug found along the way: `generate-prefs.R` emitted boolean object getters as `this.x || <default>`, so a stored `false` read back as `true` whenever the default was `true` (unchecking the old "Use device pixel ratio" checkbox never persisted). The generator now checks for a stored boolean, and the regenerated accessors fix the other true-default getters too (`enableSplashScreen`, `showWhatsNew`, the GPU options, and the pane layout's `consoleRightOnTop`).
- **Publishing**: RPubs keeps a fixed plot's size (and so its layout) too, drawing it at a lower pixel ratio when it's larger than the standard 1024 x 768 size so the page doesn't embed huge images.

## Implementation

- The RStudio graphics device (`RGraphicsDevice.cpp`) now keeps the pane size reported by the client separately from an optional fixed size. The effective size prefers the fixed one. Client metrics still save and restore the pane's size, so turning the fixed size off after a session restart doesn't leave a stale pane size behind.
- The setting is stored in a new `fixed_plot_size` user state (`{enabled, width, height, units}`). `SessionPlots.cpp` applies it at startup and on `userState().onChanged`, converting it to 96-DPI pixels and clamping it to the supported range. The plots-changed event carries a `fixedSize` flag, so the client knows how to display the image.
- `ImageFrame` can show the image at a given CSS size, scaled down to fit and centered, using pure CSS (`min()` of the plot size and the frame's viewport), so no JS resize handling is needed.

## Testing

- R (`test-graphics.R`): writing the state pins `dev.size()` in inches, centimeters, and pixels, clamps out-of-range sizes, and follows the pane again when the setting is turned off.
- e2e (`fixed_plot_size.test.ts`, desktop-dev): default state; fixed size sets `dev.size()` and keeps the aspect ratio, and a pane resize (after the metrics RPC lands) leaves the device alone; unit conversion in the dialog; out-of-range sizes are rejected and cancelling restores the menu's checked state; the export dialog defaults to the fixed size; `locator()` on a centered plot reports its center (verified to fail with the mapping disabled); Fit to Pane restores pane-sized plots.
- R (`test-graphics.R`): PNGs and JPEGs saved through RStudio's export path (`.rs.api.savePlotAsImage`) record 96 DPI; the raw Quartz output doesn't.
- R (`test-graphics.R`): `.rs.api.savePlotAsImage()` raises an R error (and writes no file) for an image that would exceed the bitmap size limit; RPubs images for a 30 x 30 in plot are 768 x 768 and 1536 x 1536.
- e2e: at a fixed 4 x 3 in, Save as Image at 300 DPI shows "4 x 3 in, 1200 x 900 pixels", disables the resolution for SVG, and writes a 1200 x 900 PNG recording 300 DPI.
- Manually: all four bitmap formats saved through Quartz now report their DPI in `sips` and in their raw PNG `pHYs` / JFIF / TIFF / BMP fields; `NSImage` (and so the macOS clipboard) sizes the fixed PNG at its physical size.
- The existing `plots_pane.test.ts` passes, including the zoom and save-image tests.
- Manually checked screenshots of the pane at small and large fixed sizes, the menu, the dialog, and the zoom window.

Not covered: Windows, the Desktop native menu's radio state (the handlers re-sync the checked state after a cancelled dialog), and pasting into Word itself (verified via the file metadata Word reads, not in Word).

Fixes #4422.

title: warn when a project asks for a different r version, and offer to switch via rig
description:
## Intent

When a project asks for a different version of R than the one running, tell the user and make switching a single click, installing that R first when it is missing. The request comes from the project's `renv.lock` (`R.Version`), or from an explicit `RVersion` in the `.Rproj`, which wins when set. Only the major.minor is compared, matching renv's own load-time check.

Fixes #12622.

## Approach

- **Session** (`SessionRenv.cpp` / `.R`): once a new session is idle after startup (or one resumed from a suspend for restart, i.e. Restart R, as renv's own check runs again then; `RInitInfo` now records which kind of suspend a resumed session came from), and again whenever a client reconnects to the running session (e.g. a browser refresh), read the requested version (the lockfile is found as renv finds it, including profiles and `RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE` directory overrides; anything that isn't a version number is ignored), compare it with the running R, and fire `project_r_version_mismatch` (which also reports an R installation in progress, so a reloaded page picks up waiting for it). Only the minimum supported R version is enforced (the maximum is a "tested with" bound), judged by the R that would actually run. When the versions agree but the renv library is empty and the lockfile records packages, fire `renv_restore_prompt`.
- **Finding and installing R** (`SessionRig.R` / `.cpp` / `.hpp`): installed versions come from rig (both modes) plus the platform's standard locations, so R installed without rig is found too; homes are derived from the layout without running R, and native arm64 builds are preferred on Apple silicon (read from `libR.dylib`'s Mach-O header). Installing runs in a Background Jobs job: download rig with curl when missing (a rig older than the pinned 0.10.0 is passed over), verify it against pinned SHA-256 digests, extract it, then `rig add <version> --user` (admin mode needs sudo, which a session child can't answer). Completion is reported through `r_install_completed`; the job can be stopped at any point. Installing is refused outside desktop mode.
- **GWT**: `RenvRVersionManager` shows the warning bar, now with an action link (`WarningBar.setAction`); everything substituted into its HTML is escaped. The switch reuses the quit path Workbench already uses (`quit_session` with an `RVersionSpec`). Once the quit is going ahead, the new `setPendingRVersion` bridge call has the desktop check that the R runs (in the background) and hold on to it for the relaunch; a quit that then fails clears it. The bar and its offer stay up until the quit goes ahead, and a failed switch shows why, with the offer to try again. A new pref, `check_project_r_version` (Global Options > Packages), disables the check. Server editions show the bar without an action.
- **Desktop**: `launchNextSession` prepares the environment for the pending R and picks the rsession build matching it on every launch (arm64/x86_64 on macOS, UCRT/i386 on Windows), since a switch can call for another one. On Windows the switch is stored as the Choose R dialog stores a choice (clearing the use-default flags), once a session has started with it, so it holds for later launches and can be changed back there. On macOS and Linux nothing is stored: the switch lasts until RStudio quits, and the bar offers it again on the next launch if the project still asks for it.
- **macOS framework installs**: every `R.framework/Versions/<v>/Resources/bin/R` launcher hard-codes the framework's Current R as its home, so querying a versioned install through it (and switching to it) silently yields the default R. `detect-r.ts` now takes the launcher's steps with the install's own `R_HOME` (source its `etc/ldpaths`, then run `bin/exec/R`), which is also what selects the `libR.dylib` rsession loads. Every R is also queried with the library path RStudio was launched with, so after a switch the previous R's library directory no longer leads the session's library path.
- **Non-orthogonal framework versions**: the CRAN installer leaves each framework version's `bin/R` (and `Renviron`, `fonts.conf`, `Makeconf`) pointing at the framework's shared `Resources`, i.e. the Current version. Even with rsession switched, every R process it starts (`R CMD INSTALL`, `renv::restore()`, callr) would run Current. The session flags such versions; switching to one first asks to update it the way `rig system make-orthogonal` does (the prompt says it affects all users of the Mac). The desktop applies the change (`r-framework.ts`) directly when the files are writable (the installer makes them writable by the admin group), otherwise through macOS's administrator authorization dialog, and it refuses to switch to a version that is still non-orthogonal.

## Verification

- `rstudio-tests --scope r --filter "rig|renv|linter"`: 200 pass (`test-rig.R` is new; lockfile and version-check tests added to `test-renv.R`).
- Desktop: `npm test` (480, including `r-framework.test.ts`, which updates a fake framework tree), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`.
- `ant draft` builds.
- New desktop-only e2e `tests/projects/renv_r_version_switch.test.ts`:
  - switching to another orthogonal R: checks the restarted session's R version, the session's own check, and the version a child R process runs;
  - declining the update of a non-orthogonal version leaves it and the session unchanged;
  - accepting the update, then switching (opt-in with `PW_ALLOW_R_FRAMEWORK_UPDATE=1`, as it edits a system-wide installation);
  - a dismissed warning comes back after Restart R, and after a browser refresh (each fails without its change; not desktop-only).
- All three pass on macOS against real CRAN framework installs: the opt-in run updated R 4.5-arm64 (its launcher now runs 4.5.3 while the default `R` still runs 4.6.1; the edited files keep their `root:admin` ownership) and switched to it, and a second run switched to the updated 4.5 and declined the update of 4.4. The files were writable by the admin group there, so the administrator-authorization path has not been exercised.
- Windows and Linux paths are untested end to end (the Windows session-binary and stored-choice unit tests run only on Windows CI).

## Not in this PR

- Workbench should map the action onto its own R version switch.
- Build tools (Rtools via rig, macOS CLT, Linux system requirements) are the planned next phase.

title: install synthetic local packages in test-install-packages.R
description:
## Intent

Make `test-install-packages.R` independent of network access and of the active set of R repositories. The first test installed rlang from CRAN and from Package Manager and downloaded tarballs from CRAN, so it failed whenever either was unreachable (most recently on the PPM line, with an empty library and a follow-on error from the DESCRIPTION read).

## Approach

- The repository, local-source, and local-binary legs now install a synthetic package built on the fly: from a `file://` repository, from its source tarball, and from a binary produced with `R CMD INSTALL --build` (still only where `.Platform$pkgType` is not `source`).
- The URL-install test for #18198 serves the tarball over `http://` from R's own help server via a custom handler in `tools:::.httpd.handlers.env`. The install hook's URL check needs a real `http://` URL and `install.packages()` doesn't accept `file://` with `repos = NULL`, so this keeps that code path covered offline. rsession points R's httpd port at its own web server (which doesn't dispatch custom handlers), so the helper starts a dedicated httpd on a fresh port and restores the original port on exit.
- The fixture helper builds tarballs with R's internal tar instead of shelling out to `R CMD build`, so it no longer assumes R is on the PATH. It moved to the top of the file since the first tests now use it.
- The Windows skips on the hook tests are dropped, since their stated reason was `R CMD build` availability. CI only runs the r scope on Linux and macOS, so these remain unverified on Windows.

## QA Notes

`./rstudio-tests --scope r --filter install-packages` on macOS:

```
[ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 40 ]
```

## Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, the NEWS file has been updated (test-only change; no entry)
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] The change is tested and works correctly

title: Scan two more UI states for accessibility and group results across states
description:
Adds two UI states to the accessibility suite and replaces the per-test Summary blocks with one report grouped across states.

New states, each in its own fresh session like the initial state:

- `packages-pane`: the initial state with the Packages pane shown in place of Files (`activatePackages`, Ctrl+7). It waits for the package list to load before scanning.
- `untitled-r-script`: the initial state with a new, empty R script open (`newSourceDoc`).

Most problems (the splitters, the Files-pane label) appear in nearly every state, so per-state reporting repeats each one per state. The merge job of an accessibility run now reads every state's `axe-results.json` (`scripts/a11y-report.ts`) and writes one Summary entry per distinct problem, a rule on one element matched by axe's target selector, listing the states it was seen in. The target is used instead of the HTML snippet because splitter snippets carry layout positions that differ between states. Incomplete results are grouped the same way in the collapsed *Needs review* section.

State names link to `a11y-screenshots.html`, a single page of every state's screenshot with the images inlined, uploaded with `archive: false` so it opens in the browser. GitHub drops `#fragment`s on artifact links, so each link opens the top of the page, which lists the states.

A state is named after its test file. The `a11yPage` fixture writes the name to the test's output dir before the session starts, so a test that fails before its scan is listed as "Not scanned" rather than silently dropped from every "seen in" list.

A pane's selected tab is client state that outlives the session and is only sent on a 5-second passive timer. The Packages state switches back to Files after its scan and, if Packages was already sent, waits for the save that replaces it. Otherwise the next state's session would open on Packages.

Harness tests in `tests/harness/a11y-report.test.ts` cover the grouping, rendering, and file reading, including duplicate state names, unscanned states, and unreadable files.

Verified with run [38637474737](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/38637474737) (daily 2026.11.0-daily+40). Every merge-job step passed and the summary step got the screenshots page URL. Per state, the scans found 3, 4 and 3 failing rules (14 nodes in all). The grouped Summary lists 5 rules and 7 distinct nodes; for example, the right and middle column splitters appear once each, seen in all three states. Locally, an extra copy of the initial state run after both new states opened on Files and found the same problems as the first, so neither state leaks into later sessions.

title: e2e: Wait for chat iframe text after restart in persistence test
description:
Fixes #19104.

`chat pane content survives R session restart` read the chat iframe's `innerText` once and asserted it was non-empty. After the R session restarts, the resumed Posit Assistant app first renders a loading skeleton with no text while it connects. The screenshots from both failing runs in #19104 show that skeleton, so a single read could catch it before any text appeared.

The test now asserts with `toHaveText(/\S/, { useInnerText: true })`, which retries until the body has text, up to `TIMEOUTS.consoleReady` (15s).

The flake predates the Posit Assistant 1.8.0 release: the Windows failure in #19104 ran 1.7.0. CI logs since 2026-09-12 show 25 failed attempts of this test, most of which passed on retry.

Local runs (10 repeats, macOS desktop) passed but never took the double-buffered resume path where CI fails, so CI on this PR is the real check.

title: Bump PATCH version for rel-blue-mistflower

title: Show a11y violation details on the run Summary page
description:
The accessibility workflow's Summary page listed one line per failing rule, so finding the offending elements meant downloading the test-results artifact and opening `axe-violations.txt`.

Each scan's Summary block now has:

- One collapsible section per violated rule. The header is the old one-line summary; expanding it shows the rule's help link, its WCAG tags, and each node's HTML snippet, failure summary, and target in the `axe-violations.txt` format.
- One collapsed *Needs review (incomplete): N* section listing axe's incomplete results in the same format. Before, only the count was shown and the details were only in `axe-results.json`. With no incomplete results it stays a plain count line.

Each rule shows at most 10 nodes, followed by "N more node(s) in axe-violations.txt" (or `axe-results.json` for incomplete results). GitHub limits each step's summary to 1 MiB and fails the upload past that; every state scanned in a run appends to the same step, so a high-count rule repeated across states could otherwise lose the whole summary. Rule lines are HTML-escaped because some axe help text contains markup (e.g. "<html> element must have a lang attribute").

Verified with runs [38608934212](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/38608934212) (built from source) and [38623659818](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/38623659818) (daily 2026.11.0-daily-40): both report the three known violations and two incomplete results, and the summary uploaded without an error annotation.

title: Update GWT to 2.13.1
description:
Addresses #19099.

Moves the GWT fork from `2.12.2-autumn-hawkbit` to `2.13.1-montauk-daisy`, built from the new [`rstudio/montauk-daisy`](https://github.com/rstudio/gwt/tree/rstudio/montauk-daisy) branch of rstudio/gwt. The tarball is uploaded to `s3://rstudio-buildtools/gwt/gwt-2.13.1-montauk-daisy.tar.gz`.

## GWT fork changes

- Merged upstream tag `2.13.1` into a branch off `rstudio/autumn-hawkbit`. The conflicts were all in upstream-owned files (Maven relocation poms that upstream deleted, sample poms, `Java17Test`, `.gitignore`). The fork's dependency bumps in the sample poms are reapplied to the per-module poms where 2.13.1 now declares those dependencies.
- Upstream 2.13.0 (gwtproject/gwt#10108) sets `role="presentation"` on the layout tables in `CellPanel`, `DecoratorPanel` and `MenuBar`, which the fork already did. The fork's duplicate calls are removed, so `CellPanel` and `DecoratorPanel` now match upstream.
- The other fork patches are carried forward unchanged: menu keyboard and ARIA changes, keyboard splitter resizing, tab context menus, and the stale-JS incremental compile fix.

The SDK has the same set of jars as before, so `src/gwt/.classpath` is unchanged. The 2.13.1 distribution no longer includes `doc/` or `samples/`, which RStudio doesn't use.

## Testing

Against the new SDK on macOS with JDK 17:

- `ant javac`: no warnings
- `ant build` (production compile): succeeds. It prints one Gin warning about `jdk.internal.reflect.ConstructorAccessorImpl`, which the 2.12.2 build prints too.
- `ant unittest`: 709 tests pass
- `ant testpage`: 677 checks pass
- `dependencies/common/install-gwt` downloads and installs the uploaded tarball, and the installed SDK is identical to the build

Still to do by hand:

- `ant devmode` session, including on Windows (the reason for 2.13.1 over 2.13.0)
- Keyboard and ARIA checks of the fork patches: menu Space/Home/End and one-level ESC, keyboard splitter resizing, tab context menus
- e2e smoke tests

title: make console output cost proportional to the output, not the scrollback
description:
Fixes #19082.

### Intent

Console output got slower as the scrollback filled, to the point of freezing the IDE: with a full 10000-line scrollback, `for (i in 1:3000) { message(i); cat(i, "\n") }` took 13-14 s. Terminal R runs it instantly, and so does RStudio with an empty console.

### Approach

Two per-chunk costs grew with the text already in the console rather than with the output being added. Both are in the client, and neither is a regex.

**1. Per-chunk line counting walked the whole scrollback, twice.** `ConsoleOutputWriter.outputToConsole()` ran `DomUtils.countLines()` over the entire `<pre>` before and after each `VirtualConsole.submit()` to learn how many lines the chunk added (there was a `TODO` asking to defer it). Every stdout/stderr switch is its own chunk, so the loop above did 12000 full walks.

`VirtualConsole` now tracks the net newlines it has written to the DOM (`getNewlinesWritten()`), and the writer takes the delta across each submit. The count is maintained at every DOM mutation the console makes: attaching a range (`countAttached`), detaching one (`removeRange`), in-place edits (`ClassRange.rewrite` / `replaceTail` / `flush`), form feed, the trimming of a condition group's leading/trailing newlines, and the truncation done when a group starts mid-line. It deliberately does not reflect what the writer's own scrollback trimming removes, since the writer already subtracts that. The count has to be exact in both directions: an over-count would make `trimExcess()` eat a real line on every condition group, so the visible scrollback would shrink a little further with each `message()`; `testTrimmingStaysExactAcrossConditionGroups` guards that.

**2. Appending a line rewrote the whole span.** `ClassRange.appendRight()` read the span's `textContent`, concatenated, and wrote it all back, twice per line (the text, then the newline). Plain stdout from one command lives in a single span, so each line copied the command's entire output so far.

Appends to the trailing range are now buffered in the range and written once per `submit()` (`flush()`, via a `try`/`finally` around the body, and before any code that reads the DOM or starts a new range). A flush extends the trailing text node while it is under 64 KB (`Text.insertData`) and starts a new text node otherwise, so edits near the end never copy more than that. Overwrites and trims near the end (`\r` progress bars, `CSI K`) go through `replaceTail()`, which edits just the trailing text node when the affected text lies within it and only falls back to a full rewrite otherwise. It addresses from the end of the text, which also keeps those edits in the right place after the scrollback limit has trimmed the front of the span.

The buffering is invisible to anything outside `VirtualConsole`: the DOM is complete at the end of every `submit()`, and `innerHTML` serialization is unchanged because adjacent text nodes concatenate (the 164 existing `VirtualConsoleTests` pass unmodified).

Normalized groups retain the count of omitted trailing newlines, so cursor edits and color-range splits keep their original columns even after scrollback trimming. Leading and trailing newline runs are trimmed across adjacent text nodes. Writes and clears inside detached groups do not affect the visible line count. Styled overwrites into ranges removed by scrollback trimming stay offscreen, without attempting to insert beside a detached DOM node or interrupting subsequent output.

### Measurements

Playwright server-dev mode, same machine, CDP CPU profile attached. "Before" is the `bugfix/console-error-key-regex` build (#19081), so the last row shows that fix in the baseline and its absence here; this branch is on `main` and the two are independent.

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `for (i in 1:3000) { message(i); cat(i, "\n") }`, full scrollback | 14129 ms | 672 ms |
| 10k short stdout lines, empty scrollback | 460 ms | 241 ms |
| 10k short stdout lines, full scrollback | 394 ms | 267 ms |
| 3k stdout lines of 120 chars, full scrollback | 416 ms | 213 ms |
| 2000 `\r` progress writes after 5000 lines | 286 ms | 230 ms |
| 5000 `\r` stderr writes (gert-like, #19081) | 183 ms | 10614 ms (regex from #19081, not in this branch) |

In the before profile, 11 of the 14 s are `countLinesInternal` and the DOM accessors it calls; after, no RStudio function appears above the browser's own `(program)` time. A 10k x 120-char variant of the third row crashed the baseline renderer during profiling and completes on this branch.

### Pre-existing bugs found by the new tests

The second commit adds a chunking-invariance test (the same stream delivered whole, in random pieces, and one byte at a time must render the same text and line count) and two seeded fuzz tests over random mixes of every escape the console understands. They found three things, all reproduced on untouched `main` in a throwaway worktree before fixing:

1. **Prompt-time edits were never counted.** `normalizePreviousOutput()` (trims a group's surrounding newlines) and `ensureStartingOnNewLine()` (may add one) change the DOM without going through `outputToConsole()`, so the writer's count drifted by up to a line per command, in the old DOM-diff code as well. The writer now takes the delta across both.
2. **Crash or lost output when a group opens mid-line.** Starting a condition group with the cursor not at the end (e.g. a `\r` progress line interrupted by `message()`) discarded the rest of the line from the DOM only, leaving a class range pointing at a detached element. A later overwrite that reached it threw `Cannot call method "insertBefore" of null` when the style differed, or was written into the detached element and never appeared when it matched. The group now truncates the buffer and ranges too, through the same path erase-in-line already used. (This is also where the whole-scrollback count would previously have silently absorbed the discrepancy.)
3. **Message text written outside its group.** The "start a new range" request set when a group opens was consumed by the next submit even if that submit held only a newline (which `newline()` never applies it to), so when the group escape arrived in its own chunk the message landed in the span before the group, unstyled. The request now carries over until text consumes it.

One known limitation is deliberately not fixed here: RStudio's own `ESC G n ;` / `ESC H n ;` escapes are not recognized as incomplete when cut off by the end of a submit, unlike CSI sequences, so a cut inside one renders its tail as text. The session writes them atomically, so the chunking test just avoids cutting there; it is noted in the test.

### QA Notes

- 27 new `VirtualConsoleTests`: appends within and across submits land in one text node; large appends start a new node; an overwrite reaching past the trailing text node falls back correctly; `getNewlinesWritten()` matches `DomUtils.countLines()` after appends, `\r` overwrites, overwrites across color ranges, erase-in-line, form feed, condition-group trimming, a group starting mid-line, and hyperlinks; minimal repros for bugs 2 and 3 above; the chunking-invariance test over 13 streams; and two 150-trial seeded fuzz tests (newline count always exact; without groups, the DOM text equals the buffer after every submit).
- 12 new `ConsoleOutputWriterTests`: the line count matches the DOM for interleaved error/output, condition groups, `\r` progress, form feed, and the prompt-time edits; trimming stays exact across 100 condition groups and across 50 prompts with a small limit; an edit at the end still lands correctly after front trimming; a 10k-line chunk is written in at most two text nodes; styled overwrites into discarded ranges neither crash nor revive discarded output, including writes across multiple color ranges.
- Nine additional regression cases cover detached-group writes and clears, preservation of visible scrollback, cursor edits after normalization and front trimming (including color changes), writes reaching an omitted newline, and leading/trailing newline runs crossing text-node boundaries.
- Three new console E2E tests exercise real R output with a full scrollback: exact retention of interleaved messages and stdout, a colored cursor edit after a large output chunk is trimmed, and a styled rewrite into discarded scrollback followed by more output. The last test fails when the detached-range fix is removed because subsequent output is lost.
- `ant unittest` passes (687 tests). The full console pane E2E suite (`tests/panes/console/`) passes in server-dev mode on the final changes: 56 passed, 4 skipped. TypeScript typechecking passes.
- An additional local randomized probe passes 600 sequences of cursor edits, condition groups, and small-scrollback trimming with the fix.

Manual check: run the two commands from the issue and confirm the loop finishes in well under a second; then `cat(sprintf("line %d\n", 1:20000), sep = "")` and confirm the console still shows exactly the last 10000 lines (Ctrl+L, then the command, then scroll to the top).

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, the NEWS file has been updated
- [x] Added tests

title: Add axe-core accessibility scans of RStudio Server
description:
### Intent

Adds automated accessibility scans of RStudio Server with axe-core, targeting WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA, to the Playwright suite in `e2e/rstudio/`. Only manually dispatched runs execute them. The only state scanned so far is the initial state: a new session with default preferences.

### Approach

- `utils/a11y.ts` wraps `@axe-core/playwright`. `runAxe` scans with all of axe's WCAG A/AA tags (`wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`); selecting by tag is what runs `target-size`, which axe leaves off by default. `PW_A11Y_EXPERIMENTAL=1` adds axe's experimental rules and filters the results back to WCAG tags. `scanA11y` attaches a screenshot of the page as scanned, `axe-results.json` and `axe-violations.txt`, adds `a11y-rules`/`a11y-incomplete` annotations, and appends a violations block to the GitHub job summary.
- Any violation fails the test. axe's `incomplete` ("needs review") results are reported and counted but never fail it.
- `fixtures/a11y.fixture.ts` gives each test a new Server session with no prefs set, then waits for `window.rstudio.ready`, the console input, and the Files pane toolbar. To support it, the spawn/connect/sign-in part of `launchServer()` moves into `openServerSession()`; `launchServer()` behaves as before.
- `PW_A11Y=1` in `playwright.config.ts` runs only `@a11y` tests, in Server mode only, without the `setup`/`auth-teardown` projects, with no retries and no Test Insights reporter. Without it, `@a11y` is excluded from every run. `utils/env.ts` adds `envFlag()`, which reads `1`/`true` as on and `0`/`false`/empty/unset as off, case-insensitively, and throws on anything else, since a workflow interpolates a false boolean input as the string `"false"`.
- The Server workflow gains `a11y` and `a11y_experimental` inputs (dispatch and call). In a11y mode it runs one shard, skips the Copilot and OP-token steps, and doesn't publish the report to S3. The new `os-test-e2e-rstudio-a11y-server-os-ubuntu-24.yml` is dispatch-only and calls it with `a11y: true`, passing only the sccache secret.
- `@axe-core/playwright` and `axe-core` are pinned exactly at 4.13.0, so the rule set only changes on a deliberate bump.

Against the in-tree build, the initial state gives the same results on four runs:

- `aria-prohibited-attr` (1 node): `aria-label` on the Files pane select-all `<label>`
- `aria-required-attr` (2 nodes): pane splitters with `role="separator"` and no `aria-valuenow`
- `image-alt` (1 node): a 2x20 `gwt-Image` with no alt text
- needs review: `aria-prohibited-attr` 1, `th-has-data-cells` 1

So the initial-state test fails until those are fixed.

### Automated Tests

- `tests/a11y/initial-state.test.ts` (`@a11y @server_only`): the scan itself.
- `tests/a11y/scan-config.test.ts` (`@a11y`): pins the rule set against a synthetic page, with a control scan proving the page triggers each rule checked.
- `tests/harness/env-flag.test.ts` and `tests/harness/a11y-report.test.ts`: untagged, so they run in the normal suite; they cover `envFlag` and the report formatting and step-summary writing.

### QA Notes

No product change. To run locally: `PW_A11Y=1 npx playwright test --project=server`. The Server workflow with `a11y` checked has not been dispatched on this branch yet. The dedicated workflow can only be dispatched once it is on `main`.

### Documentation

"Accessibility Tests" section in `e2e/rstudio/README.md`, plus tag and env-var table rows. No NEWS entry: developer tooling.

title: keep the terminal rstudio helper on the PATH after profiles reset it
description:
### Intent

On Debian, typing `rstudio <file>` in the Terminal pane launched a second RStudio Desktop instead of opening the file. The terminal `rstudio` helper (#18763) relies on the postback scripts dir being first on the PATH, but the bash hook script sources `/etc/profile`, and Debian's stock `/etc/profile` assigns PATH outright, so the helper disappeared and `/usr/bin/rstudio` won. Reproduced in Docker on Debian 12 and 13; Ubuntu 24.04 is unaffected because its `/etc/profile` never touches PATH. macOS's `path_helper` also moves the dir to the end of PATH, which only works today because nothing else named `rstudio` is installed there.

Fixes #19086.

### Approach

- The session exports `_RS_POSTBACK_DIR` alongside `RSTUDIO_TERMINAL_HOOKS` (not on Windows, where rpostback is not installed).
- The hook `.bash_profile` prepends that dir after the system and user profiles have been sourced, unless it is already first, then unsets the variable.
- The C++ PATH prepend stays, so shells that do not run the hook script (zsh, hooks disabled) keep working wherever no profile resets PATH.

Not covered: bash with terminal hooks disabled on Debian. That shell is a plain `bash --login` with no RStudio-controlled step after `/etc/profile`, so there is nowhere to restore the PATH. The same applies to a nested `bash -l` and to zsh users whose `~/.zprofile` sources `/etc/profile`. Closing that gap means the desktop binary itself deferring to the helper when launched from inside an RStudio terminal; tracked in #19098.

No NEWS entry: the feature is unreleased.

### Automated Tests

- New testthat case in `test-terminal.R` runs bash on the shipped hook script with a scratch `HOME` whose `.bash_profile` resets PATH, and asserts `command -v rstudio` resolves to the stub postback dir. It fails against the old script and passes with the new one (verified with `--scope r --filter terminal`).
- The existing e2e spec `terminal_open_file.test.ts` is the end-to-end check and keeps invoking plain `rstudio`; the Debian certification run should now pass it.

### QA Notes

On Debian 12 or 13 with RStudio Desktop installed, open a Terminal and run `rstudio foo.R`. The file should open in the source editor; no second RStudio window should appear. Also sanity-check Ubuntu and macOS, where behavior should be unchanged.

### Documentation

None needed.

title: treat the c++ standard as a minimum so builds can match a c++20 boost
description:
### Intent

Addresses #19079.

Packagers building against a system Boost that was compiled as C++20 (nixpkgs with gcc 16, Arch with `cxxstd=23`) cannot link `rsession`:

```
undefined reference to `boost::urls::grammar::detail::condition_cat'
```

Boost.URL 1.91 (boostorg/url#976) declares its error categories as `inline constexpr` header variables when compiled as C++20, and only compiles the `extern` definitions into `libboost_url` otherwise. A Boost built as C++20 therefore exports no `condition_cat`, while RStudio -- pinned to `-std=gnu++17` by both `cmake/compiler.cmake` and `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` -- still expects it. Both downstreams currently patch our CMake files to say C++20.

Reported upstream as boostorg/url#1006 (a shared Boost.URL built as C++20 with Boost's default hidden visibility exports no error categories); a fix there would make the standard mismatch harmless, but this PR is still the right thing on our side.

### Approach

Treat the standard as a minimum rather than a pin:

- `compiler.cmake` treats 17 (20 on Windows) as a floor. When `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` is not set, the floor is raised to the compiler's own default standard (`CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_DEFAULT`) when that is newer, so a plain configure with gcc 16 builds as gnu++20 and matches the distro's Boost without any patching. CMake emits the `-std` flag for `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` even when the compiler default is newer, so this has to be explicit. An explicit `-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=20` is honored as given, and values below the floor are a configure error. `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED` and `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS` are set to ON.
- The hand-rolled `-std=gnu++17` block in `src/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` is dropped; it predates `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` and always won over anything CMake added. `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED` replaces its "no C++17 support" check.
- One C++20 portability fix: `SessionPackageProvidedExtension.hpp` holds a `std::vector<FilePath>` with `FilePath` only forward-declared; libc++ in C++20 mode instantiates the vector destructor eagerly and fails on the incomplete type.

Our own builds are unaffected: a default configure of this branch produces exactly the same `-std` flags as main (gnu++17 everywhere; strict c++17 only for gtest's own sources).

### Automated Tests

No new tests; this is build configuration. Verified locally on macOS (Apple clang 21):

- default configure: identical `-std` flags to main (Apple clang defaults to gnu++14, so the floor applies)
- gcc 16 (Homebrew) on a minimal project: `-std=gnu++20` with no `-D`; `-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=17` and `=23` honored; `=14` and `=98` rejected at configure
- `-DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=20`: full `src/cpp` build succeeds; `rstudio-tests --scope core` and `--scope rsession` pass

Building as C++20 surfaces 23 `-Wdeprecated-this-capture` warnings from `core/http/StreamWriter.hpp` (`[=]` lambdas that use `socket_`); left for a follow-up since they don't fire in our default configuration.

### QA Notes

No user-facing change. Packagers can drop their C++20 sed patches once this lands.

### Documentation

None needed.

title: anchor the console error-key regex so colon-free stderr floods stay linear
description:
Fixes #19080.

### Intent

The console stalls for seconds while large amounts of colon-free stderr output arrive, e.g. the progress text from `gert::git_clone(verbose = TRUE)`. The same output written to stdout renders in a quarter of a second, and terminal R is unaffected.

### Approach

`ShellWidget.asErrorKey()` ran `replaceFirst("[^:]*:\\s*", "")` on every stderr chunk to strip an `Error in foo:` prefix. Unanchored, that pattern is retried from every position of a string containing no colon, so it is quadratic in the chunk length (9 s for a 160 KB string). A slow chunk makes the next long-poll batch larger, so chunks grow until one carries most of the output.

Two changes:

1. **Anchor the pattern** (`^[^:]*:\s*`). Semantically identical, since any match necessarily starts at position 0, and linear in the chunk length.

2. **Key lazily.** Even linear, the per-chunk ANSI strip + regex + trim + two `TreeMap` inserts (keyed by the full stripped text, so each insert compares multi-hundred-KB strings) was pure overhead: the key is only consumed if an unhandled-error event arrives before the next prompt, which never happens for progress output. The bookkeeping moves into a small `ConsoleErrorTracker` that records the raw chunk and its elements, and computes keys only when an extended error is looked up (newest chunk first, so the common case is one comparison). This also drops the second retained copy of every chunk. Pending output is capped at 256 chunks and 1,048,576 raw characters, evicting the oldest first without computing keys. The newest chunk is always retained, even if it exceeds the text budget, so a single large error can still receive a traceback.

Measured with a CPU profile of the client (Playwright server mode, same server, only the GWT bundle changed), after change 1 alone:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 5000 `\r` stderr writes | 8254 ms | 240 ms |
| 5000 `\n` stderr writes | 7650 ms | 353 ms |
| `gert::git_clone(verbose = TRUE)` | 16692 ms | 1648 ms |
| `gert::git_clone(verbose = FALSE)` | 942 ms | 985 ms |

### QA Notes

New `ConsoleErrorTrackerTests` (18 cases) cover prefix and ANSI stripping, colon-free passthrough, newest-first matching, preservation of original ANSI text, and clearing. Regression tests check both retention limits, eviction order, matching oversized newest chunks, and releasing the text budget after matching or clearing. Timed guards verify fast key computation on a 400 KB colon-free chunk and lazy recording of a flood of such chunks. `ant unittest` passes (666 tests).

Manual check: run the snippet from the issue in the console and confirm the prompt comes back promptly; then trigger an error (e.g. `stop("boom")`) and confirm the traceback widget still replaces the plain error text.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug, the NEWS file has been updated
- [x] Added tests

title: reduce blocking work during startup
description:
### Intent

Reduce startup work that blocks the R session and avoid repeating installation probes on subsequent launches. Automatic Python discovery currently runs synchronously during deferred initialization even when no Python feature is being used.

On macOS arm64, the final worktree build compared with unchanged `b2d42d0224` produced these medians across three repeated launches, after one fresh-profile launch:

| Phase | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Workbench painted, from Electron process start | 1,871 ms | 1,498 ms |
| Wait for R metadata after app ready | 375 ms | 66 ms |
| Session module initialization | 370 ms | 255 ms |
| Blocking deferred initialization | 1,698 ms | 56 ms |
| Deferred completion milestone, from process start | 4,514 ms | 2,566 ms |
| Client initialization | 122 ms | 157 ms |

Both builds used Debug rsession, draft GWT, Electron 43.7.7, R 4.6.1 and Quarto 1.10.18. Profiles were isolated and reused within each measurement. These are local timings, not a cross-platform performance guarantee. Client initialization did not improve in this comparison. The deferred completion milestone includes the existing one-second scheduled hook.

### Approach

- Run automatic Python discovery in an asynchronous child R process, with a 30-second deadline. Resolve explicit configuration immediately and discard late results after interpreter initialization or a synchronous terminal request. A terminal that needs the result before discovery finishes retains its existing synchronous fallback. A discovery that fails is recorded as "no Python" so terminals don't repeat it synchronously; one that merely times out is retried in the background the next time a terminal asks.
- Cache successful R metadata queries on disk, checking executable and installation file identity/timestamps and relevant environment variables before reuse. Keep the existing early asynchronous probe on cache misses.
- Cache successful `quarto --paths` results, keyed by installation, version and Quarto environment overrides. A hit still requires a launchable launcher, its `tools` directory and the cached directories; development versions bypass the cache, damaged or stale caches trigger the original probe, and a launcher that later fails to start drops the cache for the next session.
- Leave TeX capability checks to their existing on-demand RPC consumers, which now cache the first answer in session info and share one in-flight probe, so later editors skip the round trip. The TeX probe used to put TinyTeX on the session PATH as a side effect; deferred initialization now does that explicitly. HTML capabilities (a knitr install check costing well under a millisecond) stay in client init. These package/tool checks can change during a session, so persistent caching would be inappropriate.
- Register SQL and Stan helpers/RPCs through lazy proxies derived from each module's definitions (only definitions at the start of a line, never shadowing a helper another module already defined), and source the R modules on first use. A proxy re-issues the caller's own call against the loaded definition rather than forwarding `...`, so `substitute()`, `match.call()`, `match.arg()` and `sys.function()` behave as in a direct call. Defer the chat base-package scan until guardrails are first installed, before hooks are active.

R metadata and Quarto paths are needed for launch configuration and are stable enough to cache with invalidation. Python and authoring capabilities are optional during initialization, so they use asynchronous discovery or RPCs instead. SQL and Stan have no startup hooks and can load at first use.

### Automated Tests

Built and tested on macOS arm64; Windows and Linux remain untested locally.

- Native session build and GWT draft build passed.
- TypeScript typecheck and ESLint passed for the desktop changes.
- Electron tests: 453 passing (12 for R detection), covering R detection, disk-cache reuse, production output separators, installation changes, environment changes, symlinks, missing installations and damaged cache entries.
- Native cache and Quarto tests: 9 passing, plus `PythonDiscoveryState` (timeout retried, failure recorded, success reused) and `quartoPathsUsable` (launcher permissions, missing `tools` or resources directories) under gtest; 682 rsession tests pass.
- R integration tests: 137 passing assertions, no warnings/failures; six existing Python execution tests skipped with no configured interpreter. Covers lazy loading, retry after failed loading, SQL/Stan first use, Python configuration and chat guardrails. title: serialize nested package-list builds so the newest list is always delivered
description:
### Intent

Addresses rstudio/rstudio-pro#13167.

When the Packages pane's Package Manager metadata column is enabled, a package installed at the console can show a blank metadata cell even though the session already holds the value. Two package-list builds overlap: the DESCRIPTION scan in `.rs.listInstalledPackages()` runs long enough for R to service polled events (`R_CheckUserInterrupt` every 1000 evals -> `polledEventHandler` -> scheduled commands, and pending RPCs while the console is busy), and the PPM batch completion posted via `executeOnMainThread` builds and enqueues a package list of its own inside the outer scan. The outer build finishes last, and its older list overwrites the fresher one in the pane. The same overlap is reachable through the `get_package_state` RPC (Refresh), which then returns the older list.

### Approach

Every package-list build now goes through `PackageStateBuilder`, a re-entrancy guard around the build. A request for a `kPackageStateChanged` event that arrives while a build is already on the stack is folded into it: no nested scan, and the outer build runs again before it delivers or returns, delivering the folded event on the request's behalf (so event-only listeners such as `DependencyManager` and `FileTypeCommands` still see the change). A request that needs its own result -- the RPC, whose handler runs synchronously inside the outer scan and has to respond with a list -- scans anyway and has the outer build run again.

Re-runs are capped at three passes as a guard against a pathological stream of requests. A successful build that still has work pending at the cap retains the owed event and queues one coalesced idle refresh instead of delivering a stale event. A capped RPC returns its last scan; the deferred event supplies the fresh state afterward. An intervening successful build can satisfy the refresh before the callback runs. Failed builds retain their owed event for the next real trigger and do not schedule retries, including when the deferred build fails. Each pass continues to build directly into the caller's object without snapshot copies.

This also protects the other fields built during the scan (`loaded`, `attached`, the package set), which were exposed to the same last-writer-wins race. Reading the metadata after the scan (the issue's option 1) would only shrink the window, so it is not included.

No atomics are needed: the build calls into R via `r::exec`, so every access to the builder's state is main-thread re-entrancy, not concurrent access.

### QA Notes

The R re-entrancy itself can't be driven by the unit harness, so the decision logic lives in `PackageStateBuilder`, which takes the build as a function; `SessionPackagesTests.cpp` scripts it (each pass stamps a sequence number into the list and can re-enter the builder or fail) and covers nested event and result requests, nested and outer failures, the pass cap, and the owed event surviving a failed build. Regression tests cover a nested RPC superseding the final allowed pass for both outer entry points, an intervening RPC satisfying the deferred event, and a failed deferred build retaining its notification without requesting another automatic attempt. The session binary builds locally and all 688 C++ session tests pass.

End-to-end verification is the recipe from the issue on a Package Manager-configured box, with `Sys.sleep(1)` patched into the DESCRIPTION scan: `install.packages('abbreviate')` should keep the Score column at `high` in every run, and the pro e2e test `test_PackageManager.spec.ts` ("posit package manager with custom meta data") should pass without the Refresh workaround from rstudio/rstudio-pro#13168.
