title: Run all test scopes on Windows CI
description:
Following #18810, which added the `rsession` scope, the Windows pipeline now drops `--scope` entirely so `rstudio-tests.bat` runs every scope it supports. In practice that adds the `r` (testthat) scope; `rserver` remains a no-op on Windows because those tests aren't built there.

Windows CI now runs the same set of test scopes as the Linux and macOS pipelines.

All scopes pass locally on Windows.

Fixes #17825.

title: harden the flakes from run 34637770965; fix console keybinding race and unbounded python discovery
description:
Triage of the 9 flaky rows in PR #18789's own all-platforms run ([report](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18789/34637770965-1/all-platforms/index.html)). Two are test-side gaps, two turned out to be product bugs. A second CI run added one more of each kind, plus a launcher fix that fell out of verifying them.

## Test-side

**`code_suggestions.test.ts` (6 rows, Posit AI Pass, all four platforms).** The failure screenshots show the status bar at "Posit AI Pass: No completions available." -- the terminal state #18789 already re-requests for ghost text, but the four NES waits and `acceptNesRename` still waited blindly. The loop now lives in `SourcePaneActions.waitForSuggestion` and is used for both ghost text and NES.

The first version re-requested with `assistantRequestCompletions` for both. Run 34711642587 showed that is a no-op for Posit AI next-edit suggestions: that command only ever asks for an at-cursor completion, and its empty-result fallback to a next-edit request is Copilot-only (`shouldFallbackToNes()` is `!isPositAi`), so the loop fired twice and the status bar just re-read "No completions available" (server-1 and mac-1, both NES specs; retries in a fresh session passed in ~14s). NES waits now re-ask with `assistantAcceptNextEditSuggestion`, which with nothing on screen calls `requestNextEditSuggestions()` directly -- the same request the automatic document-change path makes. Ghost text keeps `assistantRequestCompletions`.

**`spelling_language_switch.test.ts` "rechecks an open detached editor" (desktop-linux, both attempts, and the same in #18766's own run).** The trace shows the satellite `page` event and, 70ms later, `AceEditor` throwing "No Ace editor found containing marker" -- `waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` is satisfied by the popup's initial document, and `expect.poll` propagates a throwing callback instead of retrying it (Playwright's `pollMatcher` calls the generator outside its try/catch). The spec now waits for the source-window URL and retries the whole content check with `toPass()`.

**`build_pane_testthat.test.ts` (desktop-windows).** The project switch navigated to the new session, `rstudio.nocache.js` loaded, then the main `*.cache.js` failed with `net::ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE`, leaving a blank window the bridge would never appear in. `openProject` now reloads once if `ready` has not flipped after a 20s grace period *and* the automation bridge was never installed; a merely slow session is left alone.

**`test:desktop-dev` / `test:server-dev` GWT check.** Verifying the spelling fix from a worktree launched Electron against an empty `src/gwt/www`, because the launcher's "is GWT ready" check only asked whether *any* `RStudioSuperDevMode` process existed -- one was running for a different worktree -- and then burned two 30s attempts before failing with "window.rstudio.ready never became true". `checkGwtBuildReady` now reads the checkout out of each devmode's classpath (`<checkout>/src/gwt/src` is its first entry) and only counts one for this checkout, reports others as unable to serve this tree, and exits before launching when there is no bootstrap or only a Super Dev Mode stub with no matching code server.

## Product

**`console_editor_keybindings.test.ts` "applied at startup" (desktop-linux).** Not a timing flake: after the reload, the trace shows `read_config_json` for `addins.json` and `rstudio_bindings.json` only -- `editor_bindings.json` was never read in the whole 20s retry window. `EditorCommandManager` registers its `EditorLoadedEvent` handler inside the `AceEditor.load()` callback, and `ExternalJavaScriptLoader` drains its callbacks one per scheduler tick, so the Console's editor can attach and fire the event first. `EditorCommandManager` now also loads its bindings on `SessionInitEvent` (or immediately, if Ace finishes loading after the session is already up); `rebindCommand` fires `SetEditorCommandBindingsEvent`, which live editors already honor. The first version of this PR loaded eagerly from `finishInit`, which on the server sent `read_config_json` before `client_init` had returned; the session rejected it with `INVALID_CLIENT_ID` and the client disconnected itself. That is what failed both linux-server shards and the two `DebouncedCommandTests` in the Jenkins GWT unit tests on the first CI run.

**`global_prefs_panels.test.ts` Python interpreters (server-linux).** `python_find_interpreters` never returned within 60s ("Finding interpreters..." the whole time). Discovery ran every interpreter probe and `conda env list` via `system2()` with no timeout. Each probe is now bounded (`rstudio.python.probeTimeout`, default 10s; conda gets 3x); a probe that times out is listed as invalid, and a conda timeout skips conda environments with a warning instead of failing the scan.

Fixes #18793.
Addresses #18794.

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` for e2e, `ant javac`, R parse + ASCII check; `spelling_language_switch.test.ts` green on desktop from the worktree (after `ant draft` there and a rebuilt main session -- the launcher check above is what surfaced both). The NES specs need Posit AI credentials, so their coverage comes from CI.

title: Log Electron renderer and child process failures
description:
### Intent

Renderer failures currently appear only in debug logging, where their details are replaced with `<object>`, and GPU/utility process exits are not logged. Record these failures at error level so normal desktop logs can help diagnose crashes such as #18803.

### Approach

Register application-wide `render-process-gone` and `child-process-gone` handlers before windows are created. Preserve Electron's reason and exit code, the affected renderer's web-contents ID, and child-process type and optional service names. Keep clean exits at debug level and remove the redundant generic renderer-exit handler.

### Automated Tests

Validated on Windows x64 with Electron 43.7.0:

- Five new unit tests cover renderer and GPU crashes, signed exit codes, utility service metadata, launch failures with exit code zero, and clean-exit log levels.
- Full desktop unit suite: `npm test -- --timeout 10000` — 466 passing, 13 pending. The isolated worktree uses the existing C++ build for component-path lookup; the longer timeout accommodates Windows network-path tests.
- `npm run typecheck` and ESLint on all changed TypeScript files passed.
- `electron-forge package --platform win32 --arch x64` passed.

macOS and Linux were not tested locally.

### QA Notes

On an affected Windows machine, reproduce the failure and inspect `rdesktop.log` at the default log level. Renderer failures should include `reason`, `exitCode`, and `webContentsId`; GPU/utility failures should include `type`, `reason`, `exitCode`, and any available `name` or `serviceName`. Clean exits should appear only with debug logging enabled.

The move/resize crash in #18803 has not been reproduced locally. These events can be recorded while Electron's main process remains alive; a native main-process crash may still require a crash dump.

### Documentation

Added a NEWS entry describing the additional desktop failure diagnostics.

title: open file paths in the terminal with ctrl+click / cmd+click
description:
## Summary

File paths printed in the Terminal pane (for example by `git status`, `ls`, or compiler diagnostics) can now be opened in RStudio with **Ctrl+Click** (**Cmd+Click** on macOS). A `file:line:column` suffix (also `file(line,col)` and `file#line`) opens the file at that position. Hovering a path shows a hint naming the modifier.

Fixes #18804.

## How it works

- **Detection** (`src/gwt/.../terminal/xterm/file-links.js`): an xterm.js link provider. Every whitespace-delimited token on the hovered line is a candidate (quoted tokens may contain spaces; enclosing brackets and trailing punctuation are stripped; URLs are left to the web-links addon). Wrapped rows are stitched together the way xterm's own `LinkComputer` does, so long paths that wrap still work.
- **Validation** (`process_resolve_file_paths` in `SessionConsoleProcessApi.cpp`): the session resolves candidates against the terminal's current working directory (the cwd the existing subprocess poller already reports), so only tokens naming an existing regular file are underlined. Plain words like `modified:` never light up. UNC-looking prefixes are skipped so a hover can't stall on a network lookup, and git's `a/` / `b/` diff prefixes are retried without the prefix.
- **Activation**: `activate` checks the platform modifier; a plain click still just positions/selects as before. With a line number the file opens in the source editor at that position; otherwise it opens the way a Files-pane click would (never falling back to a download).
- **xterm quirk**: the Linkifier records any provider reply against the line it is *currently* asking about, so a slow reply for a line the mouse has left would be misattributed. The provider tags requests and drops superseded replies. Resolutions are cached per line text for a few seconds (mouse sweeps), and the cache is cleared when the terminal reports a new cwd.
- **Preference**: `terminal_file_links` (default on) with a checkbox in Global Options > Terminal, separate from "Clickable web links".

## Also

- Guards the remote terminal resize against the `NaN` dimensions the fit addon reports before the renderer has measured a cell. The session rejected that request and the terminal printed a red "jsonrpc error 6 (Invalid json-rpc request)" line; this surfaced while forcing the DOM renderer in the new test but is reachable whenever the renderer is switched.

## Tests

- New e2e spec `tests/panes/terminal/terminal_file_links.test.ts`: an absolute path with a `:2` suffix opens at line 2; a relative name from `ls` resolves against the terminal cwd after `cd`. The spec forces the DOM renderer so rows are in the DOM, and drives the raw mouse because xterm's screen element sits over the row spans.
- Ran the new spec plus the existing terminal specs against a server-dev build (12 passed); `ant javac` clean; `Rscript scripts/generate-prefs.R` re-run.

title: Keep the last project when the Dock opens a projectless window
description:
Follow-up to #18786. The Dock's "New RStudio Window" asks the session for no project with `RS_INITIAL_PROJECT=none`, and the session treated that like a `--project none` scope: it went through `resolveProjectSwitch()`, which also flushes the per-user last-project path. That record is shared by all windows, so the new empty window erased the project remembered for the window it was launched from. With "Restore most recently opened project at startup" on, the original project was not reopened on the next launch if that window crashed or the empty window was quit last.

The session now handles the desktop's env-var `none` as a plain projectless start and leaves the last project path alone. The command-line scope, used by Workbench, keeps its flush. The `none` env value is only ever sent by the Dock command, so no other startup path changes.

Also on the desktop side, from the review of #18786:

- `launchRStudio()` builds the child's environment as a copy and passes it to `spawn`, instead of setting and unsetting variables in this process's own environment.
- `LaunchRStudioOptions` is a union of the three launch intents (project file, working directory, no project), so callers can't combine them, and the function branches on the intent directly.

No NEWS entry: #18786 is unreleased.

### Verification

Desktop unit tests cover the three launch intents and that an inherited project is not passed on. Lint and typecheck are clean. The session change needs a person:

1. Turn on "Restore most recently opened project at startup". Open a project and wait 30 seconds so it is recorded.
2. Right-click the Dock icon and choose "New RStudio Window". It opens with no project.
3. Force-quit RStudio (or quit the empty window last), then relaunch: the project from step 1 reopens. Before this change it did not.

Addresses #15669

title: Run the rsession test scope on Windows CI
description:
The Windows pipeline ran only the `core` test scope, so the session gtests were never exercised there. It now runs `--scope core,rsession`.

Running that scope locally on Windows turned up one failure that had to be fixed first: `SessionRTest.SysGetenvSeesCoreSetenv`.

`core::system::setenv` writes through our C runtime with `_wputenv_s` so that R's `Sys.getenv` sees variables set after R has started. That write only reaches R when R resolves `getenv()` to the same CRT module we do, and the test guarded only on `getRversion() >= 4.2`. The version rules out msvcrt builds of R, but not the debug/release split on our side: a debug build links `ucrtbased.dll` while `R.dll` always links the release `ucrtbase.dll`. Each module snapshots the Win32 environment block once, lazily, and never re-reads it, so R never sees a write into `ucrtbased`'s table. The test now skips on debug builds, and the three comments that presented the R version as the whole condition are corrected.

Locally the `rsession` scope is now 539 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed.

This turns on one additional scope rather than every class of test, so it does not close the issue.

Addresses #17825.

title: Don't prompt to save the workspace right after a session restart
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18784.

A quit, project close, or project switch issued shortly after a session restart prompted "Save workspace image to `<path>/.RData`?" even with `save_workspace` set to `never`.

The client learned the save action only from the asynchronous `save_action_changed` event, and `ApplicationQuit.saveAction_` was initialized to `SaveAction.saveAsk()` until one arrived. The action was not part of `SessionInfo`, so there was nothing else to fall back on. On the session side, `s_lastSaveAction` starts at `kSaveActionAsk` and `onClientInit` published that placeholder as-is; only the first `onDetectChanges` pass recomputed it. Every session therefore emitted `save_action_changed {action: -1}` followed by `{action: 0}`, and a close issued before that batch reached the client used "ask".

### Approach

`SessionInfo` now carries `save_action`, which `client_init` delivers before the workbench is interactive, and `onClientInit` computes the action before publishing so the event carries the real value too. Both read one function, `modules::dirty::saveAction()`, so the two channels cannot disagree.

On the client, `saveAction_` starts null and is read through a `saveAction()` accessor that falls back to the value `client_init` reported. "Ask" is now used only when the session has reported nothing at all.

### Impact

For an interactive user this was one dismissible prompt, and every path that reaches it is user-initiated (quit, restart/update RStudio, switch R version, new project, close project, switch projects) -- nothing background can trigger it. A secondary effect was silent rather than dismissible: inside the same window, Restart R derived `saveChanges` from `SAVEASK != NOSAVE`, so a restart could write `.RData` with `save_workspace` set to `never`.

Unattended automation cannot answer the modal, so the close never completed. That is how this surfaced: `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/restart-under-agent.test.ts` timed out after 30s waiting on `window.rstudio.project.isActive() === false` while the prompt sat unanswered, on six consecutive Windows runs of the Posit Assistant release gate.

This is not a regression. `saveAction_ = SaveAction.saveAsk()` dates to 2011 (`4993b7e7e3d`) and `s_lastSaveAction = kSaveActionAsk` to 2013 (`57a301581a1`), and both are present unchanged on `rel-autumn-hawkbit`. What changed was the delivery time of the first event batch, not RStudio.

### Verification

Added `e2e/rstudio/tests/projects/close_project_after_open.test.ts`, which opens a project and closes it with no console command in between, so nothing forces the R-side detect-changes pass. It asserts `save_workspace` is `never` first, so it cannot pass vacuously under `ask`, and asserts that `closeProjectIfOpen` did not have to dismiss the save prompt -- that helper sweeps the prompt away for the other project tests, so without this assertion a regression would go unnoticed. It is untagged, so it runs in normal PR CI rather than only in the release gate.

Verified on a Windows dev desktop build:

- Every `client_init` reports `save_action=0`, across the project open and the following close.
- The only `save_action_changed` events emitted are `{action: 0}`; the `-1` placeholder is gone. Pre-fix CI payloads show `-1` then `0` in every session.
- `tests/projects/` passes in full (24 passed).

The sub-second window depends on a loaded CI worker, so the original failure was not reproducible locally; the checks above verify the mechanism instead. Final confirmation is a gate run.

`closeProjectIfOpen` also now names the modal blocking a close instead of reporting a bare `waitForFunction` timeout.

### Follow-up

`DesktopHooks.getSaveAction()` has the same event-only staleness, but it is exported to JS and uncalled -- a Qt-desktop leftover. Left alone here rather than deleting an exported symbol.

title: e2e: skip ai suites when the provider service is unreachable
description:
## Intent

Make the `@ai` e2e suites skip, rather than fail, when the CI runner cannot reach the provider's service. On PR #18747's rerun (34728179667) the macOS shard failed five Posit AI code-suggestion specs with 30s ghost-text timeouts; the trace showed the assistant manifest download from cdn.posit.co timing out, the agent reporting `NotSignedIn`, and completions rejected with "Not authenticated". The credential gate passed because it only checks for a token store on disk, so an egress outage looked like a product failure.

## Approach

- `requireAiCredentials()` / `hasAiCredentials()` now also probe each provider's services from Node (`isServiceReachable`, the pattern the citations spec already uses), and skip with a reason naming the host that did not answer. The host list lives next to the provider table in `utils/ai-credentials.ts`: for Posit AI the completion/chat hosts plus the install manifest; for Copilot the GitHub API hosts.
- New `aiServiceOutageReason()` re-probes after a request through the product came back empty. `code_suggestions.test.ts` routes its ghost-text and NES waits through it, so a service that degrades mid-run skips retroactively, while a timeout with the service still answering remains a real failure.
- `PW_AI_AUTH_STRICT` makes an unreachable service fail the gated tests instead of skipping them, matching its existing meaning for missing credentials.
- The spec's `beforeAll` skips the assistant setup when the gate is going to skip the tests, since that setup can spend a minute on install prompts against a dead network.

## Automated Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `e2e/rstudio` passes.
- `aiServiceOutageReason()` exercised directly: returns `null` with the hosts up, and a skip reason naming the first unreachable host with `fetch` stubbed to fail; strict mode returns `null` (fail) as intended.
- Local `test:desktop-dev` of `code_suggestions.test.ts`: the Posit AI half skips on credentials; the Copilot half runs and fails because this checkout has no installed copilot-language-server, and the new failure path correctly re-probed GitHub and rethrew. The end-to-end happy path needs the CI agents.

## QA Notes

If the PR run's Posit AI specs skip, the reason string should name the unreachable host; if they run, nothing changes for them.

title: e2e: poll the satellite editor and the tab indicator geometry
description:
Test-only hardening for the two linux flakes in PR #18802's e2e run ([34712089464](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/34712089464)). Neither is a product regression from that PR: the first predates it and the second is a snapshot read racing a scroll animation.

## `spelling_language_switch` "clearing a project dictionary rechecks an open detached editor"

Red on both attempts on linux-desktop (every run since #18766) and, in this run, on linux-server shard 2 as well. The traces show the satellite `page` event and then, ~70ms later:

```
Error: page.evaluateHandle: Error: No Ace editor found containing marker: The colour
    at AceEditor.editorHandle (e2e/rstudio/pages/ace_editor.page.ts:112)
```

`waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` is satisfied by the popup's initial document, well before GWT mounts the editor. The marker-based lookup throws until then, and `expect.poll` propagates a throw instead of retrying it (it only re-polls matcher mismatches). Wrapped the check in `expect(async () => ...).toPass()` so the throw is retried until the editor is up.

## `highlight_active_tabs` "selection preserves tab widths and filename truncation"

Flaky on linux-server (passed on retry): the indicator came back `position: absolute` where the test expects `fixed`. The failure screenshot shows the tab strip scrolled. `DocTabLayoutPanel.ensureSelectedTabIsVisible` animates the strip when a partly hidden tab is selected, and the scroll listener keeps `docTabPanelClipped` (the absolute variant) on the panel until the tab is fully in view, so a one-shot geometry read can land mid-animation. `expectHighlight` now polls the geometry with `toPass` until it settles; the assertions themselves are unchanged.

Verified with `npm run typecheck` and both specs on desktop-dev against the worktree's `ant draft` build (14 passed).

title: Start the Dock's New RStudio Window with no project
description:
On macOS, the Dock icon's "New RStudio Window" command passed the current window's project directory as the new session's working directory. The session then opened the `.Rproj` file found there, so the new window came up with the same project as the window it was launched from.

The command now asks the session for no project explicitly, and sends no working directory, so the new window starts in the user's Default working directory (Global Options > General > Basic) with no project open. That is where the Qt versions of RStudio started these windows; those versions reopened the project as well, by falling through to "Restore most recently opened project at startup".

Two related changes:

- `launchRStudio()` clears `RS_INITIAL_PROJECT` and `RS_INITIAL_WD` before setting up the new session's environment. An instance started by opening a project keeps those set for the life of the session -- only a session restart clears them -- so they would otherwise be inherited by the spawned window.
- The project directory the front end reported to the desktop existed only to give this command a working directory, and is removed.

### Verification

Unit tests cover the launch options and the Dock menu item's handler. The Dock menu itself needs a person to click it:

1. Start RStudio and open a project. Wait 30 seconds, so the project is recorded as the last project.
2. Right-click the Dock icon and choose "New RStudio Window".
3. The new window opens with no project, in the Default working directory.

I also confirmed the session behavior directly, with a custom Default working directory and a recorded last project: the session starts with no project and honors the preference.

Addresses #15669

title: hold rpc requests until client_init has returned
description:
Follow-up to #18797, which showed how little it takes to bring a session down from the client side.

## Problem

Until `client_init` returns, `RemoteServer` has no client id, so any other RPC goes out without one. The session rejects it with `INVALID_CLIENT_ID`, and `RemoteServer.handleRpcErrorInternally` treats that code as "another client took over": it calls `disconnect()` and fires `ClientDisconnectedEvent`, which tears down the workbench. On desktop this is silent (the disconnected UI is server-only); on the server it leaves the workbench behind a glass pane.

Any early sender triggers it: an `AceEditor.load()` callback, a `Scheduler.scheduleDeferred` in an eagerly-constructed singleton, or `logException` for an exception thrown during startup. It never reproduces on desktop, where the session is up before the page loads and `client_init` returns in milliseconds, and only shows up on server CI, where `client_init` takes seconds while rserver launches the session -- and there it looks like a pile of unrelated project-switch flakes. In #18797's first run, 85 of 226 `client_init` calls on the linux-server shards had such a request racing them.

## Change

`RemoteServer.sendRequest` now holds requests while `clientId_` is null, the same way it already holds them while unauthorized, and sends them (with the id filled in) as soon as the `client_init` response arrives. `client_init` itself, `auth_status`, and `abort` (the "R is taking longer to start" dialog's Terminate R / Safe Mode buttons) still go straight out; the exemption list is a `protected` method so it can be extended. Each held request is logged via `Debug.log`, so a `client_init` race stays visible in the console without being fatal. `RpcRequest` gains `setClientId` for the replay and an `isCancelled` flag so a request cancelled while held is dropped rather than sent.

Satellite windows proxy their RPCs through the main window's `RemoteServer`, so they are covered by the same guard.

Verified with `ant javac`, and `console_editor_keybindings.test.ts` + `project_editor_theme.test.ts` on desktop against the worktree's `ant draft` build (8 passed). The server-side case is exercised by the PR-triggered linux-server e2e shards.

title: Fix Posit Assistant failing to start in a second RStudio instance on Windows
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18787. Replaces #18788, which targeted `main`; this is the same change based on `rel-autumn-hawkbit` for the 2026.09.1 patch.

On Windows, every RStudio session named its Posit Assistant "in use" lock file `pai/locks/sessions/.lock`, so a second instance collided with the first and Posit Assistant refused to start with "A Posit Assistant update is in progress".

The owner id that names the file is a function-local `static const std::string` initialized by a conditional expression. MSVC 19.51 in C++20 mode (which the Windows build uses) initializes that static to an empty string; the same code is correct in C++17 mode, as a non-static local, or when the initializer is wrapped in a lambda. The static was introduced by #18573, which is why 2026.08 is unaffected.

Upstream: this is a regression in MSVC 19.51 / Build Tools v14.51 (VS 2026 18.6+), which the Windows CI image uses via its VS 2026 18.7.3 pin; MSVC 19.29 through 19.50 compile the same code correctly. Microsoft tracks it as Developer Community ticket [11093947](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/MSVC-1451-codegen:-ternary-picks-wrong-/11093947), fixed in the v14.52 preview ([July 2026 preview notes](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/msvc-build-tools-preview-updates-july-2026/)). No GA toolset carries the fix as of 2026-09-11, so the source-level workaround is required. Details in the issue.

### Approach

- Compute the owner id inside an immediately-invoked lambda with plain locals.
- `InstallLock::acquireInUse` refuses an empty owner id with a real error, so a regression surfaces as "Unable to verify the Posit Assistant installation state" instead of silently sharing one file and reporting an update in progress.
- Expose `InstallLock::ownerId()` as a test seam.

### Automated Tests

The lock tests were entirely `#ifndef _WIN32`, so nothing exercised owner-path naming on Windows. This PR moves the tests' common includes out of the POSIX-only block and adds three tests that compile everywhere:

- the session lock file is named `<owner>.lock`
- an empty owner id is refused without creating `.lock`
- the production accessor's owner id is non-empty (fails on the previous initializer under MSVC, passes with the fix)

### QA Notes

Verified on Windows 11 with the local dev build; QA notes added to the issue.

### Documentation

None; no user-facing behavior beyond the bug fix. NEWS entry added to `version/news/os/NEWS-2026.09.1-autumn-hawkbit.md`.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: warn about non-ascii characters that look like ascii in r code
description:
## Intent

R diagnostics now warn about characters in code that look like ASCII but are not, e.g. a Cyrillic `с` where `c` was meant:

> Non-ASCII character U+0441 looks like 'c'

Fixes #14485.

## Approach

`ConfusableCharacterLinter` (new, client-side, in `views/output/lint`) runs alongside the R lint request in `LintManager` and appends warning-level lint items, so the result shows up as the usual squiggle + gutter icon + hover message. It walks the document's Ace tokens and flags:

- Cyrillic letters with a Latin lookalike (`а е о р с у х ...`);
- the Greek question mark (`;` U+037E), typographic quotes and dashes, the Unicode minus sign, the Unicode spaces (no-break, narrow no-break, en/em/thin/hair, ideographic, ...), and fullwidth ASCII forms (the usual suspects when code is pasted from the web);
- zero-width characters (ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, word joiner, soft hyphen, BOM), reported as `Invisible character U+200B` since there is nothing to see. R rejects all of these with "unexpected input", joiners inside e.g. Persian identifiers included.

Exemptions:

- Greek letters: `ρ`, `ν`, `Χ2` and friends are deliberate statistical symbols, so no Greek letter is a lookalike (the Greek question mark still is);
- backtick-quoted names, which can hold any character and usually have to match e.g. an imported column name exactly;
- string and comment tokens, roxygen comments and Quarto `#|` options included (a row whose first token is a comment is skipped whole; a `#` that continues a multi-line string is not) (formatted roxygen prose such as `**bold**` is tokenized as `constant.numeric.virtual-comment`, not `comment`);
- in R Markdown / Quarto, anything outside the body of an R chunk: prose, the chunk header row, and chunks in other engines. The engine comes from parsing the chunk header (`RChunkHeaderParser`, `engine=` overrides included) rather than from the highlighter, which falls back to R rules for engines it doesn't know such as `{markdown}`;
- tokens that also contain non-ASCII characters *without* a lookalike -- a word genuinely written in another script (e.g. the identifier `сумма`) rather than a stray lookalike. This keeps the warning quiet for Cyrillic-script users while still catching `с(1, 2, 3)` and mixed-script names like `LаTеX`.

New pref `warn_confusable_characters` (Global Options > Code > Diagnostics, under the R diagnostics options; on by default). The source file uses `\u` escapes so it stays ASCII.

Not covered: the console input (this rides on the document lint pipeline).

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/editor/confusable_characters.test.ts`: an R script with a Cyrillic `с` in code, in a string, in a comment, inside a genuine Cyrillic identifier, plus an en dash in formatted roxygen prose, a no-break space, a zero-width space, a multi-line string whose closing row starts with `#`, a backticked column name with a curly apostrophe, and a Greek `ρ` assignment, yields exactly the expected warnings (four, with their rows, columns and messages); turning the pref off removes them. An R Markdown document with lookalikes in prose, in a `#| fig-cap:` line, and in `{r}`, `{asis}`, `{markdown}`, `{python}` and `{r, engine='python'}` chunks yields exactly one warning, at the `{r}` chunk row. `global_prefs_panels.test.ts` and `rmarkdown.test.ts` still pass locally in desktop-dev mode.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test
- [x] `Rscript scripts/generate-prefs.R` run for the new pref

title: keep a minimized console pane minimized after a successful render
description:
## Intent

Keep a minimized Console pane minimized after a successful render. Failed R Markdown renders open the pane so their output can be inspected. Explicit Console activation, including Ctrl+2 and sending code to the Console, keeps the pane open across later renders.

Fixes #11622.

## Approach

- Tag frame requests that automatically restore a minimized pane and track them in `LogicalWindow`.
- Restore minimization when a successful background task returns control through `ConsoleActivateEvent(false)`. This covers R Markdown, Quarto preview, Compile PDF, and deployment completion.
- Clear automatic-raise tracking after explicit Console activation or code execution, including when the pane is already visible. Explicit Console-pane activation also clears it.
- Explicitly activate the Console pane after an R Markdown failure so the Render output is visible.

## Testing

- Java compilation and a GWT draft build passed.
- E2E TypeScript typecheck passed.
- The three Console render tests and the existing pane-layout and R Markdown suites passed in desktop-dev mode.
- Console render coverage includes successful and failed renders from a minimized pane, and successful rendering after restoring the Console with Ctrl+2. Tests wait for the session's render-completed event and its UI processing rather than checking the runner's filesystem, so they do not require local access to rendered files.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry with issue link
- [x] e2e tests

title: make the document outline available for markdown documents
description:
## Intent

Plain Markdown (`.md`) documents get the document outline, like `.Rmd` and `.qmd` already do: the Outline toolbar toggle, the heading tree, and the current-section indicator in the editor status bar.

Fixes #13505.

## Approach

- `mode/markdown` (`src/gwt/acesupport/acemode/markdown.js`) now constructs the same `RCodeModel` the R Markdown mode uses, over its own tokenizer. The code model's chunk start/end patterns are set to never match, since plain markdown has no code chunks, so the scope tree consists purely of headings. Highlighting is untouched. The code model is only created when a session is supplied (the mode constructor is also used as a prototype base by `rmarkdown.js`).
- `WebContentFileType` passes `canShowScopeTree = isMarkdown`, so the Markdown file type offers `toggleDocumentOutline` (HTML stays as is).

This is the "switch the file type to R Markdown" workaround from the issue, minus the side effects of actually being an R Markdown document.

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/editor/markdown_outline.test.ts`: for a `.md` with `#`/`##`/`###` headings, the outline command is enabled and the section scopes nest by heading level (`Two` under `One`, `Three` under `Two`, `Four` top-level). `code-folding.test.ts` and `rmarkdown.test.ts` still pass locally in desktop-dev mode.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test
- [x] `ant acesupport` run for the mode change

title: render quarto documents without a preview server when no preview is requested
description:
## Intent

With the Quarto preview option set to **(No Preview)**, Render now runs a one-shot `quarto render` instead of `quarto preview`. The Background Jobs pane shows a "Render: file.qmd" job that finishes when the render does; no preview server is left running.

Fixes #12838.

## Approach

`QuartoPreview` gains a render-only mode, chosen in its constructor when the effective viewer type is `none` (the same pref the gear menu's "(No Preview)" sets):

- `args()` becomes `render [file] --to <format>`; for a project directory it renders the project.
- `name()` is "Render: ..." rather than "Preview: ...".
- `onCompleted()` calls `activateConsole()` on success, mirroring what the preview does once its server is up. A failed render leaves the job output in front; error navigation into the source (`navigateToRenderPreviewError`) is unchanged since `onStdErr()` still runs.

The existing reuse path in `quartoPreviewRpc` requires a live server port, so render-only jobs are never reused; each Render starts a fresh job (after stopping any running preview, as before).

This deliberately keeps the existing "(No Preview)" setting as the switch rather than adding a separate "render as job / in console" option; the issue's ask was specifically that "No Preview" should not leave a server behind.

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/editor/quarto_render_no_preview.test.ts`: with `rmd_viewer_type = none`, rendering a chunk-less qmd produces the HTML, and the Background Jobs pane shows a "Render: ..." job in the Succeeded state and no "Preview: ..." job. `quarto.test.ts` (the preview-to-Viewer flow) still passes locally in desktop-dev mode against a worktree build of rsession.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test

title: add smooth scrolling option for the source editor
description:
## Intent

A "Use smooth scrolling" option (Global Options > Code > Display, off by default) makes the source editor animate scrolls that it initiates itself, e.g. when the cursor moves off screen or on Go to Line, instead of jumping.

Fixes #14696.

## Approach

Ace already has this as `animatedScroll`, and `Renderer.setAnimatedScroll()` was already wrapped but unused. The new `smooth_scrolling` pref is bound to every source editor in `TextEditingTargetPrefsHelper`, next to `scroll_past_end_of_document`, so it applies live to open documents and to documents opened later. Mouse-wheel scrolling is native and unaffected; the visual editor uses a different engine and is out of scope (as the issue notes).

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/editor/smooth_scrolling.test.ts` checks the active editor's `animatedScroll` option follows the pref live and that a newly opened document picks it up. `global_prefs_panels.test.ts` still passes locally in desktop-dev mode.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test
- [x] `Rscript scripts/generate-prefs.R` run for the new pref

title: apply the console scrollback limit immediately
description:
## Intent

The console scrollback limit -- Global Options > Console, now labelled "Maximum lines of output to keep in the console" -- takes effect as soon as it is changed, instead of at the next session start. This is the knob the issue asks for (a configurable, large scrollback); it existed but was easy to miss and appeared not to work because nothing applied it live.

Addresses #16386. The "practically infinite" variant is not implemented: the session's console-actions store is a `boost::circular_buffer` sized to the limit, so an unbounded buffer would need a different store; very large finite values are accepted as before.

## Approach

- `SessionConsole.cpp`: the capacity setup moves into `applyConsoleMaxLines()`, called at init and from a `userPrefs().onChanged` handler when `console_max_lines` changes (same minimum-of-10 guard as before).
- `Shell.java`: follows the pref live via a value-change handler, mirroring the session's minimum, so the client trims (or stops trimming) on the next output. The initial value still comes from `SessionInfo`.
- `ConsolePreferencesPane`: the numeric field's minimum is 10, matching what the session accepts, so a value it would silently ignore can no longer be entered. Label reworded (en/fr) since "console history" reads as command history.

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/console/console_max_lines.test.ts`: lowering the limit to 50 and printing 200 lines leaves at most the tail in the console; raising it to 5000 keeps all 200 -- with no restart in between. `console_pane.test.ts`, `console_output.test.ts` and `global_prefs_panels.test.ts` still pass locally in desktop-dev mode against a worktree build of rsession.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test

title: add select current statement command
description:
## Intent

**Code > Select Current Statement** (default shortcut `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S`, also in the Command Palette) selects the whole R statement containing the cursor, however many lines it spans -- the selection counterpart of Execute Current Statement.

Fixes #16102.

## Approach

`EditingTargetCodeExecution` gains `getCurrentStatementRange()`, which is the range Execute Current Statement runs (`getMultiLineExpr` bounded to the chunk body when inside one), without the up-to-10 comment lines that command also folds in above the statement. `getRangeFromBehavior()` now builds on the same helper (the chunk row-limit logic moved into `getRowLimits()`), so the two commands cannot drift apart. The new `selectCurrentStatement` command has `context="r"` like `executeCurrentStatement`, and `TextEditingTarget.onSelectCurrentStatement()` applies the range as the selection through `withVisualModeSelection`.

The shortcut is free on all platforms in the default, Vim, Emacs and Sublime keymaps.

## Testing

New Playwright test `tests/panes/editor/select_current_statement.test.ts`: from the middle of a seven-line `ggplot() + ...` call the command selects exactly those lines; on a one-line statement it selects only that line; inside an Rmd chunk it selects the multi-line statement and nothing outside the chunk. Passes locally in desktop-dev mode; `execute_from_editor.test.ts` also passes (the shared range helper was refactored).

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test
- [x] Commands.cmd.xml.MD5 updated

title: highlight only the active document tab, including its top border
description:
### Intent

Follow-up to #18734. Two changes to the active tab highlighting:

- Only the active document tab is highlighted. Pane tabs (Environment, Files, and so on) and minimized pane strips return to their previous styling.
- The indicator now includes the top border of the selected tab: a flat 3px bar along the tab's top edge that curves down into the tab's rounded corners, painted over the pane frame's border line rather than sitting beneath it.

Addresses #18692.

### Approach

The pane frame paints a 1px border across the top row of the tab strip, and the strip is deliberately offset 1px above its GWT layout layer, which clips it. So the tab's top row is never visible and nothing drawn in flow inside the tab can reach it. The indicator is therefore drawn "by hand" from the tab's client rectangle using CSS anchor positioning: the selected tab carries an `anchor-name`, and its `::before` is a `position: fixed` box anchored to the tab with `top`/`left`/`right` from `anchor()`. A fixed box escapes every ancestor's overflow clipping, and anchor positioning keeps it attached through resizes, drags and strip scrolling. `anchor-scope` binds each overlay to its own tab when several source columns each have a selected tab, and `position-visibility: anchors-visible` hides it if the tab is scrolled out of the strip.

The overlay is shaped like the top of the tab (3px top border, 1px side borders, a radius 1px larger than the tab's so the curves stay concentric), so the flat top and the end curves come from a single painted shape with no seam. An inset box-shadow could not do this because it paints inside the border box while the bar fills it.

The anchor rules live in an `@supports` block, which GWT's legacy CssResource parser passes through verbatim; only `@external` class names are used inside it. Browsers without anchor positioning keep an in-flow `position: absolute` version of the same shape as a fallback (clipped at the tab's top row, as before).

A fixed box is not clipped by the strip, so while the selected tab is only partly in view the bar would spill past the strip edge. `DocTabLayoutPanel` listens for scrolling on the strip's layout layer and re-checks after selection and resize; while the tab is partly hidden (past either edge, or under the utility area) it sets `docTabPanelClipped` on the panel, and the stylesheet returns the overlay to the in-flow shape so the strip clips it along with the tab. Selecting the tab scrolls it back into view and restores the anchored overlay.

The dark theme accent changes from `#8ab4f8`, which was nearly as light as the tab label and read as a highlight rather than an accent, to `#4586e2`. The preference title becomes "Highlight active document tab"; generated accessors and `NEWS.md` are updated to match.

### Automated Tests

- `highlight_active_tabs.test.ts` was rewritten for the new behavior: it reads the `::before` overlay via `getComputedStyle`, checks its shape, that it is `position: fixed` and starts 1px above the tab, checks the accent per theme (Modern light, Modern dark, Sky), and asserts pane tabs and minimized strips are never highlighted regardless of the preference. Preference default/Cancel/Apply/reload persistence and stable tab widths under selection are retained.
- A test opens 20 files, scrolls the selected tab half out of the strip, and checks that the panel is flagged and the overlay falls back to `position: absolute`, then that selecting the tab restores the anchored overlay.
- 8 tests pass on macOS Desktop (`test:desktop-dev`, retries disabled). `panes.test.ts` (37) and `active_tab_restore.test.ts` (2) also pass against this build. Playwright typecheck and GWT draft build pass.

### QA Notes

Open a few documents and switch between them; the selected document tab should show a blue bar along its top edge that covers the pane's grey border line and curves into the tab's corners. Pane tabs should look exactly as they did before #18734. Check Modern light, a dark editor theme, and Sky. Disable "Highlight active document tab" under Global Options > General > Basic > Other and confirm the bar and label emphasis disappear.

With many documents open, drag a tab toward the strip edge so the strip auto-scrolls and the active tab ends up partly hidden; the bar should be cut off with the tab rather than continuing over the overflow buttons or the pane border.

title: deny duplicate named windows before electron creates them
description:
## Intent

`Application.windowCreated()` handles Electron's `did-create-window` event. When the pending window's name was already tracked, it raised the existing window and returned early, intending to "deny" the new window. But by the time `did-create-window` fires the `BrowserWindow` already exists, so the early return orphaned it: never configured, shown, tracked, or destroyed, and still carrying its frame name, so `activateWindow(name)` could match the orphan instead of the intended window.

## Approach

Move the duplicate-name check into `windowOpening()`, the `setWindowOpenHandler` callback, where returning `{ action: 'deny' }` stops Electron from creating the window at all. A denied request never reaches `windowCreated()`, so the pending entry is consumed there too; otherwise it would linger and attach to the next unrelated `window.open()`.

This mirrors the old Qt `WebPage::createWindow()`, which returned `nullptr` in the same situation. The GWT desktop window opener already tolerates a null `window.open()` result (`DesktopWindowOpener.showPopupBlockedMessage()` returns false), and `SatelliteManager` re-activates known satellites before opening, so this remains a last-resort guard.

## Verification

Three new unit tests in `application.test.ts` cover the satellite deny, the secondary-window deny (both activate the existing window and empty the pending queue), and the allow path leaving the pending entry queued for `windowCreated()`.

From `src/node/desktop`: `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 478 passing, with only the known worktree-only `findComponents` failure (no built rsession).

No NEWS entry: the path is rarely reachable in practice since Chromium reuses same-name windows for `window.open()` from the same opener.

Fixes #18775.

title: Backport e2e flake hardening to rel-autumn-hawkbit
description:
Backports af7ab6b5ef (#18789) from `main`. That commit hardened five specs
traced to specific races in a cross-platform run; four of them apply here.

- `resetToUntitled` kept a dirty untitled placeholder. The placeholder is
  shared across specs, so text a previous spec left in it survived the reset;
  the next `saveAllSourceDocs` then raised a modal Save File prompt for the
  pathless doc, and its glass panel blocked every later click.
  `SourceColumnManager` now only reuses a clean untitled doc,
  `waitForSourcePaneReset` requires one, and `closeSourceAndDeleteFile` drops
  the `saveAllSourceDocs` it never needed (the file is deleted on the next
  line). Adds `source_pane_reset.test.ts`, which fails without the
  `SourceColumnManager` change.

- `closeProjectIfOpen` could sit behind "Save workspace image?". The sessions
  run with `save_workspace: never`, but `ApplicationQuit`'s `saveAction_`
  holds its `saveAsk()` default until the backend's `SaveActionChangedEvent`
  lands, so a project closed seconds after it opened prompts anyway.
  `dismissSaveWorkspacePrompt` clears it.

- The vimrc mid-session spec clicked the editor straight after
  `newSourceDoc`, which only dispatches the command, so the click landed on
  the outgoing document's unrendered `ace_content`. Waits for the new editor.

- The ghost-text specs treated "No completions available" as something to
  wait out. It is terminal -- nothing re-asks -- so a declined suggestion
  cost the full 30s budget. Re-requests instead.

## Notes for review

The fifth spec in #18789, the console-keybindings startup race, is omitted:
its feature (#18761, custom editor keybindings in the console) is not on this
branch, so neither is the spec. That was the only cherry-pick conflict; the
rest applied byte-identical to `main`.

This carries one non-test change, `SourceColumnManager.onDocumentResetToUntitled`.
`DocumentResetToUntitledEvent` is dispatched only from `ApplicationAutomation`,
the `window.rstudio` automation bridge, so no user-reachable path sees the
changed behavior. The accompanying `isDirty(EditingTarget)` extraction
preserves the existing `dirty != null && dirty` logic.

`source_pane_reset.test.ts` lands on a branch that does not have the stale
source column fix (#18736 / #18737, currently `main`-only). The dirty-untitled
case routes into the existing create-then-close path, which never reaches zero
tabs -- the state that bug needs -- and that path already runs on this branch,
so the two should not interact.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` and `ant javac` both clean. The specs themselves have
not been run on this branch.

title: add change spelling language command; apply dictionary changes live
description:
## Intent

Switching the spelling dictionary takes one step and takes effect immediately:

- **Edit > Change Spelling Language...** (also in the Command Palette) opens a small picker with the installed dictionaries (plus the usual "Install more languages..." entry) and applies the choice on OK.
- Dictionary changes -- from that dialog, from Global Options > Spelling, or from Project Options > Spelling -- now re-check open documents right away. No restart.

Fixes #12223.

## Approach

Two things made the old flow need a restart:

- `RealtimeSpellChecker` registered a no-op handler for `spelling_dictionary_language` changes and kept per-session `correctWords` / `incorrectWords` caches, so a stale "misspelled" verdict survived the switch. It now clears both caches and re-checks the document (`invalidateAllWords()`) when the language changes.
- `SpellingPreferencesPane.onApply()` flagged a language change as requiring a desktop restart; that flag is dropped (custom-dictionary edits keep it).

The new `changeSpellingLanguage` command is handled in `WorkbenchScreen` next to `showSpellingOptions`; `ChangeSpellingLanguageDialog` reuses `SpellingLanguageSelectWidget`. The dialog persists whichever layer is currently in effect, so the picker and the server agree afterwards:

- With no project override, it writes the global user pref and leaves the project alone.
- When the project sets its own dictionary, it rewrites `SpellingDictionary:` in the `.Rproj` (the same write Project Options > Spelling performs) and leaves the global pref alone. Note that this produces a diff in the `.Rproj` if it is under version control.

Follow-up commits on this branch harden the live update:

- `SpellingService` re-checks only after the server confirms the pref or project-config write, and tags in-flight `check_spelling` / suggestion requests with a dictionary generation so a slow response from the old dictionary is retried rather than cached.
- Full pref-layer updates (`full_layer`) replace the layer wholesale in every editor window, so clearing a project override falls back to the global default instead of leaving a stale project value behind.
- The installed-dictionary metadata returned by "Install more languages..." is written back into the shared `spellingPrefsContext`, so a reopened picker lists the new dictionaries.

## Testing

New Playwright suite `tests/panes/editor/spelling_language_switch.test.ts`:

- opens an Rmd containing "colour", confirms the realtime checker flags it under en_US, switches to en_GB through the dialog and sees the flag disappear without a reload, then switches back and sees it return;
- with a project that sets `SpellingDictionary: en_US`, switches via the dialog and checks the `.Rproj` now reads `SpellingDictionary: en_GB`;
- delays the old dictionary's `check_spelling` response and confirms it cannot restore stale results;
- clears a project dictionary and confirms an open detached editor is re-checked;
- installs more dictionaries and confirms they remain listed when the picker reopens.

New GWT unit tests in `PrefsTests` cover full-layer replacement. `rmarkdown.test.ts` and `global_prefs_panels.test.ts` still pass locally in desktop-dev mode.

## Checklist

- [x] NEWS.md entry
- [x] e2e test
- [x] Commands.cmd.xml.MD5 updated

title: Backport Posit Assistant e2e fixes to rel-autumn-hawkbit
description:
Backports three e2e-only commits from `main`. The release branch's test runs
install the latest Posit Assistant release, so without these the Posit
Assistant suite fails on 1.4.0 and later.

- `9bae5ac43f` Match chat messages by role testid, not `data-message-id` (#18781).
  PA 1.4.0 added a per-turn footer that carries `data-message-id` and renders
  after the message row, so `messageItem.last()` resolved to a cost and timing
  row instead of the reply. Matches the `ChatMessage` row wrapper and the
  `MessageRenderer` content div instead, and routes the two inline
  `[data-message-id]` locators in `conversation-history` through the page object.

- `904450a2c7` Tolerate U+200E in the skill-selection e2e assertion (#18782).
  PA 1.4.0 prefixes every tool-call caption with LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK, which
  JavaScript's `\s` class does not match, so the assertion failed against a
  rendered string that is visually identical to what it expected. The character
  class also accepts the bare whitespace 1.3.1 and earlier emit.

- `230931063e` Keep a slow Posit AI sign-in from failing the whole shard (#18780).
  A slow redirect after submitting the password was classified as a credential
  failure, which failed the auth setup project and left every dependent test as
  "did not run". Clicks with `noWaitAfter` so the 30s URL wait owns that budget,
  and treats the step as fatal only when the page shows a rejection message.
  Also widens the readline-notification test's settle window and has its prompt
  require the `executeCode` tool.

The first two match against both the currently released assistant and 1.4.0+,
so the suite passes whichever version a build pulls.

Cherry-picked clean with no conflicts. `npm run typecheck` passes in
`e2e/rstudio`, and `playwright test --list` enumerates all 84 Posit Assistant
tests.

title: e2e: harden five flaky specs from the cross-platform run
description:
The all-platforms Playwright run on #18786 ([report](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18786/34627740555-1/all-platforms/index.html)) reported 13 flaky tests across 6 files, with no hard failures. Five of the six files had a specific, identifiable race; this addresses those.

Several of them failed on **all four platforms at once**, which is the tell that they aren't timing noise -- they are state or protocol races that resolve the same way everywhere.

### 1. `resetToUntitled` kept a dirty Untitled placeholder (`markdown.test.ts`, all 4 platforms)

The failure surfaced as `focusConsole: console input did not hold focus ... something is stealing focus`. The screenshot shows why: a modal **Save File - Untitled1** dialog, holding `ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()` -- the last fixture from `ggplot_pipe_insert.test.ts`, which ran earlier in the same worker.

`resetSourcePaneState` keeps one Untitled tab open so the source pane never transits the zero-tab HIDE state (#17738), and it reuses whichever untitled doc is already open. `revertUnsavedTargets` only reverts *file-backed* editors, so a dirty placeholder carried the previous spec's text across. The next `saveAllSourceDocs` then prompted Save As for that pathless doc, and its glass panel blocked every later click.

- `SourceColumnManager.onDocumentResetToUntitled` now only reuses a **clean** untitled doc; a dirty one is closed with the rest and replaced (the existing create-then-close path already avoids the zero-tab gap). This event is only dispatched by the automation bridge, so it is test-facing only.
- `waitForSourcePaneReset` requires the settled doc to be clean, so a reuse regression fails loudly instead of silently.
- `closeSourceAndDeleteFile` drops its `saveAllSourceDocs` + `sleep(1000)`. The file is deleted on the next line, so the save changed nothing -- it was purely the thing that could raise a modal.

New spec `source_pane_reset.test.ts` covers the invariant; verified it fails (`dirty: true`) with the `SourceColumnManager` change reverted and passes with it.

### 2. `closeProjectIfOpen` waited behind "Save workspace image?" (`restart-under-agent.test.ts`, macOS + Windows)

`page.waitForFunction(() => project.isActive() === false)` timed out at 30s. The screenshot shows a **Close Project / Save workspace image to .../.RData?** prompt.

The sessions all run with `save_workspace: never`, so this looks impossible -- but `ApplicationQuit.saveAction_` is initialized to `SaveAction.saveAsk()` and only reaches the real value when the backend pushes `SaveActionChangedEvent`. A project closed seconds after it opened decides the quit inside that window and prompts. This spec closes projects in a tight open/close loop, so it lands there.

`dismissSaveWorkspacePrompt` (in `modals.page.ts`) clears it. It polls rather than waiting a fixed interval: in the common no-prompt case the quit proceeds instead, which flips `window.rstudio.ready` false or tears the context down, so a session that isn't going to prompt costs one poll.

`openProject` needs no equivalent -- the bridge fires `SwitchToProjectEvent` with `forceSaveAll=true`, which short-circuits before the prompt.

### 3. Editor keybindings load after `ready` (`console_editor_keybindings.test.ts`, Linux)

The startup spec reloads, waits for `window.rstudio.ready`, and presses the rebound shortcut. `ready` means R's deferred init finished; it says nothing about `EditorCommandManager`, which loads `editor_bindings.json` on `EditorLoadedEvent` through a separate async file read. The press can land before the rebinding exists and is swallowed (the console held `gamma delta`). Now the set/press/assert block is wrapped in `toPass()`, so the retry is the wait -- and a binding that never arrives still fails.

### 4. Clicking the editor before `newSourceDoc` produced one (`vimrc_keybindings.test.ts`, Windows)

`locator.click: Element is not visible` on `.ace_content`, with `force: true`. `force` skips the actionability checks, not the scroll-into-view that a zero-box element fails -- the click landed on the outgoing document's `ace_content`, still in the DOM but no longer rendered. `executeCommand(page, 'newSourceDoc')` only dispatches; the document is created over an RPC. Both tests now wait for the new editor to be active and painted. (The first test only passed because a polling assertion sat between the two steps.)

### 5. "No completions available" is terminal, not slow (`code_suggestions.test.ts`, all 4 platforms)

The status bar in the failure snapshot reads **"Posit AI Pass: No completions available."** -- the request completed with nothing. Nothing re-asks from there, so `toBeVisible({ timeout: 30s })` waited out the full budget for a suggestion that was never coming. That is a live model declining a context, and it declines the same context on every platform, which is how one empty answer became four flaky rows.

`expectGhostText` now re-issues `assistantRequestCompletions` when the status bar reports an empty response, and still fails if nothing ever arrives.

### Not changed: `rmarkdown.test.ts` "empty chunk does not define variables" (server-linux)

This one is not a test bug. The trace shows, right after `restartRRunAllChunks`:

```
Event listener stopped due to error (code=2, attempt=0); scheduling revival
WARNING: Error connecting with session.
1: jsonrpc error 1 (Unable to connect to service)
```

The session stayed unreachable for the whole 60s budget (revival cadence is 5s, so ~12 failed attempts), the console never got past `Restarting R session...`, and the toolbar was still showing the Session Suspended icon. The test's comment says its tight budget is deliberate -- it is the canary for #18340 -- so loosening it would hide exactly what it exists to catch. Leaving it to keep reporting.

### Verification

`npm run test:desktop-dev` on macOS, against a worktree `ant draft` build:

- `source_pane_reset.test.ts` -- passes; fails with the `SourceColumnManager` change reverted
- `ggplot_pipe_insert.test.ts` + `markdown.test.ts` + `source_pane_reset.test.ts` in order (the sequence that produced the flake), `--workers=1` -- 20 passed
- `vimrc_keybindings.test.ts` + `console_editor_keybindings.test.ts` -- 8 passed
- `projects/ignorefiles.test.ts` + `projects/project_editor_theme.test.ts` (close-project path) -- 7 passed
- `math_preview` + `rnotebook` + `notebook_inline_chunks` + `multiline_chunk_execution` (a sample of `closeSourceAndDeleteFile` callers) -- 11 passed

`code_suggestions.test.ts` needs AI credentials and can only be exercised in CI.

title: Fix Posit Assistant failing to start in a second RStudio instance on Windows
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18787.

On Windows, every RStudio session named its Posit Assistant "in use" lock file `pai/locks/sessions/.lock`, so a second instance collided with the first and Posit Assistant refused to start with "A Posit Assistant update is in progress".

The owner id that names the file is a function-local `static const std::string` initialized by a conditional expression. MSVC 19.51 in C++20 mode (which the Windows build uses) initializes that static to an empty string; the same code is correct in C++17 mode, as a non-static local, or when the initializer is wrapped in a lambda. The static was introduced by #18573, which is why 2026.08 is unaffected.

### Approach

- Compute the owner id inside an immediately-invoked lambda with plain locals.
- `InstallLock::acquireInUse` refuses an empty owner id with a real error, so a regression surfaces as "Unable to verify the Posit Assistant installation state" instead of silently sharing one file and reporting an update in progress.
- Expose `InstallLock::ownerId()` as a test seam.

### Automated Tests

The lock tests were entirely `#ifndef _WIN32`, so nothing exercised owner-path naming on Windows. This PR moves the tests' common includes out of the POSIX-only block and adds three tests that compile everywhere:

- the session lock file is named `<owner>.lock`
- an empty owner id is refused without creating `.lock`
- the production accessor's owner id is non-empty (fails on the previous initializer under MSVC, passes with the fix)

### QA Notes

Verified on Windows 11 with the local dev build; QA notes added to the issue.

### Documentation

None; no user-facing behavior beyond the bug fix. NEWS entry added.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md`
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets [accessibility standards](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Accessibility)
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)

title: e2e: keep a slow posit ai sign-in from failing the whole shard
description:
## Intent

Two hardening changes prompted by the e2e failures on #18765, none of which were caused by that PR.

## Approach

**Auth setup (`tests/auth.setup.ts`).** The `submit password` step was marked fatal, so any error there became a `LoginAutomationError` and failed the setup project, which left every dependent test in the shard as "did not run" (333 tests on the Linux server shard). The actual failure was a slow redirect after the click, not a rejected password: `click()` waits for the navigation it triggers under the runner's `actionTimeout`, which is 10s here (the runner applies the config's `actionTimeout` to contexts launched during a test, contrary to the comment that assumed a 30s library default).

- Click with `noWaitAfter` so the existing 30s `waitForURL` owns the redirect budget.
- Classify by error kind rather than by step: the step is fatal only when the login page shows a visible rejection message (an `alert` role or narrow text such as "incorrect" / "invalid"). A stalled redirect now falls through to the transient path, and the `@ai` tests skip with that reason in the status file rather than taking the shard down.
- `step()` keeps a `LoginAutomationError` a step throws itself, so the fail-loud verdict for a real credential problem survives.

**Readline test (`readline-notification.test.ts`).** Its post-readline idle wait was the only 30s turn budget in the suite; every other wait settles for at least 60s. The assistant routinely keeps working after `readline()` returns (reads the console back, comments on the result), which is what failed on both macOS and Windows.

- Raise that wait to 90s and set the test timeout to 300s so two turns plus the readline fit.
- Spell out in the prompt that the code must be run with the executeCode tool and not written to a file, which is what the first macOS attempt did (the notification never appeared).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio` passes.
- Neither path can be exercised locally without Posit AI credentials, so verification of the live behavior is via CI on this PR (the `@ai` suite and the auth setup run there).

## Checklist

- [x] No NEWS.md entry (test-only change)
