title: Report why a Posit Assistant package download failed
description:
`downloadPackage()` downloaded the Posit Assistant package with an in-process `download.file()` call that dropped the reason for a failure, ignored the return status, and passed a `timeout` argument `download.file()` does not have. This is the install/update counterpart of the manifest fix in #18578.

The download now runs through `.rs.chat.downloadPackage()`, which:

- collects `download.file()`'s warnings with `withCallingHandlers()` and folds them into the reason it returns, so the cause of a proxy, DNS, or TLS failure -- which `download.file()` puts in a warning while its error says only that the URL could not be opened -- reaches the install dialog and the session log. The warnings are collected but not muffled, so they still reach the console as they do for any other download.
- checks the return status. `download.file()`'s libcurl and internal methods can report a failure with a warning and a non-zero status rather than an error (curl and wget `stop()`), and a truncated package that passed the empty-file check previously reached the SHA-256 verification and was reported as a package integrity failure.
- sets `options(timeout = )` -- the documented transfer-timeout knob -- to at least 60 seconds, without shortening a longer value configured by the user or administrator. The old `timeout = 60` argument landed in `download.file()`'s dots and was discarded.

The helper returns the reason as a string (`""` on success), which `downloadPackage()` turns into an error. The method itself is still left to `options(download.file.method)` / `download.file.extra`, as before.

`performInstall` builds its message with `core::errorDescription(error)` instead of `error.getMessage()`. `systemError(code, description, location)` records the text as the error's `description` property and leaves `getMessage()` as the bare errno string, so the message would otherwise have read "Download failed: Input/output error" -- and "Download failed: Protocol error" for a non-HTTPS package URL. `core::errorDescription` prefers the description and falls back to the message; it is the accessor the manifest download failure path already uses.

## Not addressed

With `options(download.file.method = "curl")` -- a configuration corporate proxies do use -- `download.file()` runs curl through `system()`, so curl's diagnostics go to the console and the error R raises is the reason-free `'curl' call had nonzero exit status`. Those users get no cause in the dialog. Capturing the child's stderr (as `.rs.air.downloadFileWithCurl` does) would fix that and is left for follow-up.

## Testing

Seven tests in `src/cpp/tests/testthat/test-chat.R`, alongside the existing `manifestDownloadCommand` tests that cover the same two behaviors for the manifest fetch. They stub `download.file` through a child of the helper's closure environment and cover a successful download, a non-zero status reported with only a warning, an error whose cause is in a preceding warning, warnings still surfacing to the caller, a warning promoted to an error under `options(warn = 2)` being reported once, and the timeout floor being applied and restored (including restoring an unset timeout to unset).

    ./build/src/cpp/rstudio-tests --scope r --filter "chat|linter"   # FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 244

The install dialog text has no automated coverage -- `downloadPackage` and `performInstall` are file-local statics in `SessionChat.cpp` with no seam for one -- so the end-to-end message needs manual verification. To reproduce a failure locally, point the session at an unreachable proxy (`https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:9`) and trigger an assistant install or update: the dialog and the log should now name the cause rather than reporting "Input/output error".

Addresses #18610.

title: Fold a section header decorated with hashes as top-level
description:
Folding a section header decorated with a run of `#` characters collapsed far more of the file than the section it labels -- often everything through several later sections, or the whole rest of the document.

Hierarchical section folding, added in 2026.05.0 (#17388), infers a header's heading level by counting its leading `#` characters. A bar like `##############` is *nothing but* leading `#` characters, so its width was read as its heading depth: a 14-hash bar became a level-14 heading, a 26-hash bar a level-26 heading. A fold runs until it reaches a header at the same level or shallower, so a wider bar later in the file looked like a subsection and was folded away along with its contents.

## What changed

Heading level is now inferred in one place, `sectionHeadDepth()`, read by both the document outline and section folding:

- a header made up entirely of delimiter characters carries no heading level -- its width is decoration;
- neither does one whose run is deeper than `######`, matching what the outline already did on the grounds that HTML only provides `<h1>` through `<h6>`;
- otherwise the level is the length of the leading `#` run.

A header with no heading level is top-level: folding treats it as level 1, and the outline records it as a plain section that closes every open section scope rather than only the innermost one. Folding reads the header out of the sectionhead token rather than the physical line, as the outline does, so a header preceded by code (`x <- 1 ## Section ----`) gets the same level in both.

| header | fold | outline | before |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `##############` | flat | flat | fold read it as level 14 |
| `####====` | flat | flat | fold flat, outline h4 |
| `###----` | flat | flat | fold 3, outline h3 |
| `### ----` | 3 | h3 | unchanged |
| `##### A #####` | 5 | h5 | unchanged |
| `########## B ##########` | flat | flat | fold read it as level 10 |
| `x <- 1 ## S ----` | 2 | h2 | fold read it as top-level |

`#` / `##` / `###` hierarchies continue to nest, and the `hierarchical_section_folding` preference still turns hierarchical folding off entirely.

The `> ######` rule is a heuristic, not a banner detector: it works because decorative runs are usually wide, but it cannot tell `###### Six ######` from a genuine `<h6>`. That case nests as it always has, and folding and the outline agree on it.

## Testing

Five new tests in `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/editor/code-folding.test.ts`, each confirmed to fail before the corresponding change:

- bars of hashes, and of mixed delimiters, fold flat regardless of width;
- a banner header does not fold away a wider banner below it;
- a depthless header is top-level in the outline, not nested under a preceding `#`;
- a header preceded by code folds at its own heading level.

Verifying the outline half needed a `getSectionScopes()` helper on the `AceEditor` page object, since `getScopeTree()` returns only the root's direct children.

Also run: the three pre-existing folding tests, 28 scope-tree-adjacent editor tests (editor, markdown, rmarkdown, quarto, sweave, rename-in-scope, rmarkdown chunks), and `ant testpage` (677 assertions).

Fixes #18602.

title: Generalize the Windows executable signing comment
description:
Rewords the comment above the `Sign Executables` stage in `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.windows` so it no longer names specific signing-operation counts.

The counts tracked the length of the `EXECUTABLES` list, so they go stale whenever that list changes, and they are already wrong in rstudio-pro, which signs an additional license-manager binary. The comment now describes the same tradeoff -- the executables account for nearly all of a build's signing operations, hourly builds sign only the installer -- without the numbers.

Comment-only change; no behavior difference.

title: Mark RPubs and ShinyApps.io as deprecated in publishing UI
description: RPubs and ShinyApps.io now carry a `[Deprecated]` suffix wherever they appear as publishing destinations: - **Publish wizard** -- the RPubs service page and its caption (`PublishDocServicePage`, `PublishRPubsPage`). - **Publish to RPubs dialog** -- title and header (`RPubsUploadDialog`). With publishing to Posit Connect disabled, the Publish button skips the wizard and opens this dialog directly, so it needs its own marker. - **Connect Account dialog** -- the ShinyApps.io account page (`NewRSConnectCloudPage`). RPubs is not listed here, since publishing to RPubs does not use an account. - **Account lists** -- ShinyApps.io accounts in the publish dialog and the Publishing options pane (`RSConnectAccountEntry`). The suffix comes from one translatable message per bundle, `deprecatedServiceLabel` (`{0} [Deprecated]`), rather than being baked into each label. `RSConnect.SHINY_APPS_SERVICE_NAME` is unchanged, as it is also matched against an account's server name. Subtitles and body text are left as they are; the bracketed marker is the whole notice, as requested in the issue. ### Verification Manual, against a dev RStudio Server build: - Tools > Global Options > Publishing > Connect... shows `ShinyApps.io [Deprecated]` alongside Posit Connect and Posit Connect Cloud. - Plots pane Publish, with Connect and external publishing enabled, shows `RPubs [Deprecated]` in the Publish To wizard. - Plots pane Publish with "Enable publishing to Posit Connect" unchecked opens the RPubs dialog with `Publish to RPubs [Deprecated]` as both its window title and its header. - The Publishing options account list shows a ShinyApps.io account as `garytr: shinyapps.io [Deprecated]`, and a Posit Connect account unchanged as `gary: connect.posit.it`. ### Notes Two known limits, both deliberate: - **Account row width.** The marked server text measures 151px (vs 73px unmarked) at the account list's 12px font. The Publishing options list is 300px wide and a marked row measures 218px there. The publish dialog's list and "Publish to account:" box are 250px (`RSConnectDeploy.css`), leaving room for a ShinyApps.io account name of roughly ten characters before the row overflows and the list -- already `overflow: auto` -- scrolls horizontally. Those widths are left alone rather than widening the publish dialog for every user to fit a marker on a service being retired. - **Wizard page element ids.** `WizardPageSelector` derives each page's DOM id from its title, so the RPubs and ShinyApps.io page ids change (`rstudio_label_rpubs_wizard_page` -> `rstudio_label_rpubs_deprecated_wizard_page`) and, since the marker is translated, now vary by locale -- as they already do for the pages whose titles were localized. No test or product code keys off these two ids. Previous deployments listed in the Publish dropdown (`DeploymentMenuItem`) are not marked. Addresses #18605. ## screenshots

title: Sign only the installer on hourly Windows builds
description:
Hourly Windows builds now spend one code signing operation instead of ten.

A Windows build signs ten things: the nine executables named in the `EXECUTABLES` environment of the `Sign Executables` stage, plus the NSIS installer in `Sign Installer`. Each file is a separate signing operation. This gates the nine on `params.DAILY`, so hourly builds skip them while daily and release builds keep signing everything we ship — release builds route through the daily pipeline, so they pass `DAILY=true` too.

The installer keeps its signature on every build, hourlies included. It is the artifact SmartScreen and the UAC elevation prompt key off, so the download-and-install experience for an hourly does not change. The unsigned payload binaries surface only as "unknown publisher" in the first-launch firewall dialog.

The DigiCert tool install, `healthcheck`, `keypair ls`, and certificate download move into a new `Prepare Signing Tools` stage that runs for every build. None of those consume a signing operation, so hourlies still exercise the signing credentials and catch a rotation or an expired certificate rather than leaving it for the next daily. Running the stage ahead of `Build` also means a credential problem fails in about a minute instead of after a full build, which is what the adjacent `Validate Signing Credentials` stage was already there for. `certsync` stays in the signing stages, next to the `signtool` calls whose cert store it prepares.

### Why this is safe to skip on hourlies

Nothing in the build depends on those signatures:

- `package/win32/make-dist-packages.bat` just runs `cpack -G NSIS` / `-G ZIP`. It neither verifies nor re-signs anything; signing ran first only so the installer would embed already-signed binaries.
- The product performs no Authenticode check at runtime — no `WinVerifyTrust`, no `windowsSign` in the Electron forge config, no auto-updater.
- `Jenkinsfile.pull-request*` never builds Windows, so no other Jenkins pipeline consumes these signatures.
- The GitHub Actions Windows e2e workflow is unaffected: it resolves the daily manifest, never an hourly, and its `build_from_source` path already installs an entirely unsigned Windows build.
- `clean-build.bat` only removes `package/win32/build`, so the `cert.pem` now downloaded before `Build` survives it.

### Verification

No Groovy or Jenkins linter is available for this repo, so this has had review only. It needs a manual `windows-pipeline` run to confirm:

- `DAILY=false` — `Prepare Signing Tools` runs, `Sign Executables` shows as skipped, `signtool verify` on the installer passes.
- `DAILY=true` — both stages run, as before.

A signed build on demand still works without a new parameter: run the pipeline manually with `DAILY=true`.

No `NEWS.md` entry — this is build tooling, not product behavior.

Addresses #18513.

title: Resolve the NES language server through the assistant installation lookup
description:
`paiLanguageServerPath()` hardcoded `<XDG_DATA>/pai/bin/dist/nes`, so the language server behind Posit Assistant code suggestions ignored both `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` and system-wide installs. The chat backend honors both, since it resolves through `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`.

Two divergences followed:

- With only a system-wide install (`/etc/rstudio/pai/bin`), chat worked and code suggestions never started. The failure logged at debug level only, so it was invisible unless assistant logging was turned up.
- With `RSTUDIO_POSIT_AI_PATH` pointed at a dev build, chat ran the dev build while the language server came from whatever was in the per-user install, with nothing reporting the mismatch.

`paiLanguageServerPath()` now derives its directory from `locatePositAssistantInstallation()`, so both halves of the assistant resolve the same installation. The lookup within an installation is split out as `nesLanguageServerPath(installPath)` and covered by tests: empty install path, an installation with no NES script, resolution under an arbitrary install root, the `language-server.js` fallback, and the `.cjs` preference.

One behavior change worth noting: `locatePositAssistantInstallation()` accepts an installation only when the chat files are present (`dist/client/index.html`, `dist/server/main.js`), so a directory holding `dist/nes` alone no longer resolves. Shipped packages contain both.

Fixes #18597.

title: ci(jenkins): narrow the platform re-checkout and restore full history
description:
Two related Jenkins fixes. They are together because applying either one alone leaves the builds broken in a different way.

## Narrow the platform re-checkout

The platform Jenkinsfiles re-checkout the build commit after the pipeline's own checkout, and did so with no clone options — fetching every branch and every tag with no depth limit.

That was harmless while the job-level clone was equally broad. The clone was narrowed to the branch being built on 18 August, so the re-checkout became the first thing to pull other branches. On the pro side that made git chase submodule pointers belonging to branches the build has nothing to do with, and the checkout failed outright.

It also removes a large redundant fetch from every platform build.

## Restore full history properly

The version is derived by counting commits between a fixed base commit and the commit being built. Much of that range sits on history merged in from release branches rather than on the branch's own direct line.

The helper that restores history after a shallow clone asked for everything newer than a date cutoff. A date cutoff deepens **incrementally rather than completely**, and a single pass does not cover the range. Nothing fails, because counting commits across a truncated range returns a smaller number rather than an error — the wrong number just gets published.

Whether a pipeline is affected comes down to how many times it happens to call that helper:

- **Twice** — the platform pipelines here — end up with enough history by accident and report correctly.
- **Once** — the builders — do not. The hourly builder has been reporting `+66` where the true value is `95`.

The three platform pipelines are correct by luck. Nothing guarantees two passes is enough; it depends on the shape of history and will silently stop being enough.

Unshallowing reaches the whole range in one pass regardless of how many times the helper is called.

## Why both changes belong in one PR

Narrowing the re-checkout removes the broad fetch that was incidentally supplying the missing history. Landing it alone would give the platform builds wrong version numbers here, exactly as it did on the pro side — three pro platform pipelines are publishing wrong versions right now for this reason.

Landing the history fix alone would leave the submodule problem waiting for whenever the narrowing arrives.

## Verified

Reproduced against a clone configured the way these pipelines are:

| | build number |
|---|---|
| after the shallow clone | 66 |
| after one pass of the date cutoff | 66 |
| **after unshallowing** | **95** |

95 is correct. Confirmed afterwards that only the built branch was fetched, so the narrowed refspec is preserved and no other branches come back. Unshallowing took about 14 seconds here, measured off-agent.

## Relationship to rstudio-pro

These files are shared with rstudio-pro, where both changes are already applied. The changed lines are textually identical in both repositories, so the next upstream merge should resolve cleanly rather than conflicting or reverting.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Say what each cache seed maintains in the sentinel's alert
description:
The sentinel writes the same hardcoded sentence into every alert it files: "its build caches on main can go stale or evicted, and PR builds for that platform run cold."

That's right for the per-OS build seeds, but wrong for `os-cache-seed-e2e-deps.yml`, which runs no build at all. It warms the `os-e2e-deps` test-dependency caches -- the R library, the pak download cache, and the Playwright browsers. Anyone reading #18569 was told to go look at build caches that seed never touches.

This picks the impact sentence per seed, so the alert names what actually went cold.

title: Fix the macOS job in the e2e deps cache seed
description:
The `macos-desktop` job in `os-cache-seed-e2e-deps.yml` has failed on every run since the workflow was added in #18550. `rig add 4.5.3` succeeds, but the following `rig default 4.5.3` fails with "R version 4.5.3 is not installed": rig names macOS installs by arch and major.minor (`4.5-arm64`), not by the requested patch version.

The macOS 14, 15, and 26 e2e workflows already work around this by querying rig for the just-installed name. This applies the same approach to the seed, gated to macOS so the Linux jobs -- which register the full version and pass today -- are untouched.

Consequence of the failure: the `macOS-macos26-arm64-*` cache keys were never written on main, so the macOS 26 e2e job restores nothing and reinstalls its R packages and Playwright browsers on every PR run. The sentinel also redispatched the seed every two hours, since the keys never appeared.

Verified by dispatching the workflow on this branch: all four seed jobs pass, `rig ls` reports `* 4.5-arm64  (R 4.5.3)`, and the macOS job computes the `macOS-macos26-arm64-r-4.5-`, `-pak-4.5-`, and `-pw-` prefixes the sentinel checks. Cache saves are gated to main-scoped runs, so the keys are only warmed once this merges.

Addresses #18569.

title: Sample Node 24 action pins in the macOS 15 e2e workflow
description:
GitHub is retiring the Node.js 20 runtime that JavaScript actions declare in their own `action.yml`. The runner reads that field before running a step and posts a deprecation annotation naming the action, so every job calling one of these prints a warning today, and the step stops working once the runtime is removed.

Across `.github/` there are 160 such call sites in 15 files spanning 8 actions. Rather than bump all of them at once, this changes one call site per action type in a single low-traffic workflow, so a real run can confirm Node 24 works here before the rest follow.

The 8 pins, all in `os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml`:

| Action | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save` (the matched `tools-cache` pair) | v4.3.0 | v5.0.0 |
| `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` | v4.3.1 | v6.0.0 |
| `actions/checkout` | v4.4.0 | v5.0.0 |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4.4.0 | v5.0.0 |
| `actions/download-artifact` | v4.3.0 | v7.0.0 |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4.6.2 | v6.0.0 |
| `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` | v2.9.4 | v3.0.0 |

Each target is the first major of that action to run on Node 24, deliberately not the latest. The later majors are ESM rewrites, and `download-artifact@v8` turns a download digest mismatch from a warning into a run-failing error.

The other 13 call sites in this file stay on v4 on purpose, so the run exercises mixed versions: a v7 download reads blob reports that v4 uploads wrote, which a uniform bump would never test.

Two of the sites were chosen to cover couplings rather than just to be few:

- `cache/save` reads `cache-primary-key` from its paired `cache/restore`. That output is what all 21 save steps in the repo depend on.
- The sticky comment reads `artifact-url` from the `upload-report` step. The repo reads that output in 7 places and only one of them guards against an empty value.

No inputs, conditions or step names changed, and `node-version: 20` is untouched. The Node that Playwright runs on is a separate question from the runtime the runner uses to execute actions.

One gap worth naming: all 21 cache saves in the repo are gated on `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, so the `cache/save` site cannot be exercised from a branch. Its restore half verifies on a branch run, but the save half only proves out after merge.

Addresses #18587.

title: Truncate assistant agent stderr in logs and startup error
description:
When a bundled JS agent (Copilot or Posit Assistant language server) crashes at startup, Node.js prints the offending source line before the stack trace. That line is the entire minified bundle, so `onStderr` in `SessionAssistant.cpp` wrote ~19 KB of JavaScript per chunk into `rsession-$USER.log`, and accumulated the same text unbounded into `s_agentStartupError`, which reaches the user through the launch-failure message and the agent diagnostics output.

Stderr text is now bounded to 4 KB wherever it is logged or accumulated, keeping the tail — where Node.js puts the error and stack trace — and prefixing a `[... N bytes truncated ...]` marker. Truncation never cuts mid-way through a UTF-8 character, since the text is embedded in JSON. Specifically:

- Each chunk logged from `onStderr` (including the stale-generation debug log) is truncated to its tail.
- `s_agentStartupError` is now an `AgentStderrTail` accumulator that keeps a bounded raw tail plus a cumulative dropped-byte count, assembling the marker only when read — so the reported count stays accurate across multiple chunks.
- The Posit Assistant chat backend's stderr log in `SessionChat.cpp` (an even larger bundle, ~594K-character lines) is truncated the same way.

`AgentStderrTail` and the one-shot `agentStderrTail()` helper are exposed from the module header and covered by unit tests in the `rsession` gtest scope.

Fixes #18451.

title: Keep one titled chat iframe during Posit Assistant resume
description:
### Intent

Fixes #18585.

After an R session restart with the Posit Assistant chat pane open, the workbench DOM could hold two `iframe[title="Posit Assistant"]` elements at once, for as long as 15 seconds. Any lookup of the chat iframe by title was ambiguous for that window -- which is how `chat-pane-persistence.test.ts` failed on #18578 with a Playwright strict-mode violation resolving both frames.

### Approach

`ChatPane.loadUrlFromSuspended` double-buffers the resume: it attaches a second hidden frame, loads the resume URL into it, and removes the old frame only once that load fires (plus `FRAME_SWAP_DELAY_MS`), falling back to reclaiming the pending frame after `FRAME_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` if the load never completes. Both frames were constructed with the "Posit Assistant" title.

The pending frame is now created untitled and gets its title inside the swap branch, in the same synchronous block that makes it visible and removes the old frame -- so the DOM never exposes two frames under that name, and the visible frame always carries the title. The timeout path discards the untitled frame and keeps using the already-titled original, so exactly one titled iframe survives either way.

The double-buffering itself is unchanged: the user still sees preserved chat content under the suspended overlay while the resumed frame loads, and the 15s fallback still recovers a stalled load.

No user-visible behavior changes. The pending frame is `visibility: hidden`, which excludes it from the accessibility tree, so the ambiguity was never exposed to assistive technology -- it affected DOM lookups only. On those grounds there is no `NEWS.md` entry.

### Automated Tests

`chat-pane-persistence.test.ts` ("chat pane content survives R session restart") now:

- tags the pre-restart iframe and waits for the resume swap before sampling the frame body, so it checks the resumed frame instead of the preserved pre-restart content;
- records the high-water mark of titled iframes across the restart with a `MutationObserver` and asserts it stays at one, so re-titling the pending frame fails the test rather than only surfacing as a flake;
- counts iframes under the chat pane's panel as well, and annotates the run when the resume never double-buffered. With Posit Assistant not installed, `ChatPresenter` caches no URL and so neither dims the pane on suspend nor reloads it on resume -- a legitimate environment in which the guard proves nothing, and one that a hard "a second frame appeared" assertion would fail.

Verified with `ant javac` and `tsc --noEmit`. The Playwright test has not been run against a live IDE; that needs a Desktop build with Posit Assistant credentials.

### QA Notes

Open the chat pane, restart R, and confirm the pane still shows its content through the resume and lands on a working chat frame. To see the window this fixes, delay the restarted session's chat backend and inspect the DOM during the resume: there should be exactly one `iframe[title="Posit Assistant"]` at all times.

### Documentation

None -- no user-facing behavior change.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` (n/a -- no user-visible symptom; rationale above)
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR (if unsure who to assign, check Area Owners list)
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: e2e: forbid the assistant from overriding the shiny viewer pane
description:
In the linux-desktop E2E run on #18574 ([job link](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31929144011/job/95122883568)), the R Shiny tip-calculator test failed on both attempts waiting for the Viewer pane iframe, which never left `about:blank`. The page snapshots captured in `error-context.md` show why: the assistant prefixed `runApp()` with its own launcher override, a different one each attempt --

- attempt 1: `options(shiny.launch.browser = .rs.invokeShinyWindowExternal)` (external browser)
- retry: `options(shiny.launch.browser = .rs.invokeShinyWindowViewer)` (separate window)

Either override beats the `shiny_viewer_type = 'pane'` pref the test configures, so the app genuinely started (the console showed `Listening on ...`, and the assistant emitted the success marker) but never rendered in the Viewer pane the test asserts on.

This extends the prompt to explicitly forbid setting `options(shiny.launch.browser)` or passing a `launch.browser` argument, and pins the generated filename to `app.R` so the suite's existing `unlink("app.R")` cleanup removes the file the assistant writes (it previously chose names like `tip_calculator_app.R`, which leaked into the sandbox home).

Verification: `npm run typecheck` in `e2e/rstudio` passes. The behavioral change can't be exercised locally on this machine (no Posit AI credentials, so the test skips); this PR's own linux-desktop E2E job runs the test with real credentials.

title: treat EPERM as alive in the pending-launch liveness probe
description:
Follow-up to #18573, which added a liveness guard in `ServerSessionManager::removePendingLaunch`: a request error no longer erases the pending-launch record while the launched session process is still alive. The guard probes liveness with `core::system::isProcessRunning`, which returned `kill(pid, 0) == 0` -- but on a root-launched multi-user server, rserver's request-handling threads run privilege-dropped (`temporarilyDropPrivileges` leaves ruid 0 and euid `server-user`, and the euid transition clears the effective capability set, so no `CAP_KILL`), and `kill(pid, 0)` fails with EPERM for every live rsession owned by another user. The guard read that as "not running", erased the record on the error path exactly as before #18573, and the #18572 double-launch/orphan race remained reproducible in precisely the deployment class it targets. Dev and e2e servers were unaffected (rserver and its sessions share a uid there), which is why #18573's verification passed.

`isProcessRunning` now counts EPERM as proof the process exists -- only ESRCH means it is gone. That is the established polarity for cross-user liveness probes (psutil's `pid_exists`: "EPERM clearly means there's a process to deny access to"; moby's `process.Alive` on macOS is `err == nil || errors.Is(err, unix.EPERM)`), and the #18573 guard is the function's only caller.

Verification:

- New tests: `PosixTests.IsProcessRunningDetectsLiveAndDeadProcesses` (core) and `SessionManagerTest.RequestErrorKeepsPendingLaunchOfOtherUserProcess` (rserver). Both probe pid 1, which always exists and is owned by root, so an unprivileged test run exercises the EPERM path (and a privileged one still passes); the new rserver test fails against the previous probe.
- `rstudio-tests --scope core`: all pass. `--scope rserver`: all `SessionManagerTest` pass; the `SqliteDBActiveSessionStorageTest` failures are environmental on this machine and identical on main's build (same as noted on #18573).

No NEWS entry: this completes the unreleased #18573 fix, whose #18572 entry already covers the user-facing behavior.

Fixes #18572.

title: Surface Posit Assistant manifest error detail in log and dialog
description:
Failed Posit Assistant manifest downloads showed a generic errno string ("Input/output error" on Linux/macOS, "Access is denied" on Windows) in both the Connection Error dialog and the session log. The actual cause -- captured from the download child's stderr -- was stored on the error as its `description` property, which `getMessage()` does not return.

The fetch-error and unsupported-info consumers in `SessionChat.cpp` now read errors with `core::errorDescription()`, which returns the description and falls back to the message for errors without one, so the captured detail (e.g. `status was 'Couldn't resolve host name'`) reaches both the log and the dialog.

Regression from #17896: the previous synchronous fetch surfaced the R error text via `rCodeExecutionError`, which stores it in the error's message.

Verified manually: with a bogus `https_proxy` set in the session and Posit Assistant uninstalled, the Connection Error dialog and the `Failed to download manifest` log line both show the full download error (`cannot open URL ... status was 'Couldn't connect to server'`) instead of the generic errno text. There is no automated test: the consumer path (`onUpdateCheckComplete`) has no unit-test seam, and the existing Playwright coverage drives these dialogs through the `chat_set_update_check_override` RPC, which bypasses the fetch.

Fixes #18570.

title: Fall back to source when an e2e required package has no binary
description:
The `os-e2e-deps` action installs the harness's required-packages set into the
cached R library and hard-gates on completeness. That install forced
`type = "binary"` on every platform whose `.Platform$pkgType` is not `"source"`,
and a binary-only install never falls back on its own. PPM publishes no R 4.1
arm64 binaries for `devtools`, `reticulate` or `shinytest2`, so the gate failed
outright on the `macos14` certification cell, before RStudio was ever exercised:

    Error: [os-e2e-deps] failed to install required-packages: devtools, reticulate, shinytest2

The certification matrix hardcodes an R version per environment, and that is how
this surfaced: `macos14` is pinned at 4.1.3. It is not certification-specific,
though. Every e2e engine takes an `r_version` input, so any of them hits this when
dispatched at an R without full binary coverage. The scheduled callers simply all
pass `release`, where the binaries exist.

Retry just the packages a binary install leaves behind, from source. Cells with
full binary coverage compile nothing and behave exactly as before, and source-only
platforms (all Linux, Fedora) still make a single install call, unchanged. All three
packages support R 4.1, so the compile is viable rather than a different failure.

The same idiom, with the same missing fallback, existed in two harness copies --
`fixtures/r-libs-setup.ts` and `actions/console_pane.actions.ts` -- so both get the
retry too. Those matter for local runs on an older R: the harness resolves macOS
and Windows packages from CRAN, which publishes no arm64 binaries below R 4.2 at
all, so its own self-heal path could not heal.

Verified on a Yellow Yarrow certification run of the `macos14` cell at R 4.1.3,
where the dependency step now succeeds:

    [os-e2e-deps] installing required-packages: devtools, remotes, reticulate, shinytest2, styler
    [os-e2e-deps] no binary for: devtools, reticulate, shinytest2 -- retrying from source

`remotes` and `styler` came from binaries; the other three compiled. The remaining
test failures on that cell are pre-existing and unrelated to provisioning.

Addresses #18584.

description:

### Intent

These four files also live in rstudio-pro, where the same edits are in rstudio-pro#12292. The Open Source File Check on that PR flagged them, so this PR lands them here first to be pulled back through `upstream/pull-upstream`.

Part of rstudio/rstudio-pro#10798 and rstudio/rstudio-pro#10799 (epic rstudio/rstudio-pro#10794). Debian 12 removal is tracked in rstudio/rstudio-pro#12259.

title: Add Posit Assistant pre-release manifest gate for Desktop E2E
description:
## Summary

- Adds an opt-in `posit_assistant_test_manifest` input to the five Desktop E2E engines (Linux, macOS x3, Windows). When set, a workflow step writes `.prefs.local.json` and points `PW_RSTUDIO_PREFS_OVERRIDE` at it -- the same mechanism used for manual local testing today. Off by default everywhere; never becomes the suite default.
- Adds `os-test-e2e-rstudio-posit-assistant.yml`, a weekly Sunday 20:00 UTC caller that installs the latest daily and runs the `@ai` suite against the pre-release Assistant manifest, on one engine per platform: Ubuntu 24 (x86_64), macOS 26 (arm64), and Windows Server 2025 (the CI stand-in for Windows 11).
- Adds two checks to the worker-scoped session fixture (`rstudio.fixture.ts`): confirms the live session actually applied the requested manifest (fails loudly instead of silently testing the released Assistant), and records the installed Assistant version -- both no-ops unless the manifest was requested.

Addresses #18477. Server mode is out of scope here (blocked on #17520, since `PW_RSTUDIO_PREFS_OVERRIDE` isn't wired for Server).

title: Move the Posit Assistant gate back to Sundays at 20:00 UTC

title: Fix macOS e2e cache architecture collision and cold-build timeout
description:
Both macOS E2E engines shared a single R-library cache key (`runner.os`, which is just `macOS` for both). Because macOS 26 is arm64 and macOS 15 is x86_64, the x86_64 job restored the arm64 job's `pak`/`cli` binaries and couldn't load them ("incompatible architecture"), dying at the "Install e2e test dependencies" step. This scopes each engine's cache by OS and architecture (`macos15-x86_64`, `macos26-arm64`) via the `os-e2e-deps` action's existing `cache-scope` input, matching the pattern the Linux engines already use.

Also raises the macOS 15 `build` job timeout from 90 to 180 minutes. The Intel runner is the slowest builder in the fleet, and a cold sccache can push a from-scratch compile past the 90 minutes that suffices for the faster arm64/Linux runners, the same headroom already granted to windows-2025. Addresses #18359.

Both cache-scope changes were verified green on macOS 15 and macOS 26 via a temporary push-triggered validation workflow, removed before merge.

title: Add a macOS 15 x86_64 E2E engine and wire it into the scheduled rotation
description:
## Summary

- Runs `rig default` under sudo in the new engine; the Intel runner skips the permission-fix pass that `rig add` performs on arm64, so the unprivileged default switch fails without it
- Adds its cache-seed companion workflow

- Adds its cache-key prefixes to the eviction sentinel
- Validated with two full pre-merge runs on the real macos-15-intel runner: latest daily build and build-from-source, both passing

title: fix macOS 15 x86_64 GWT cache path and harden the seed sentinel
description:
### Intent

The cache-seed sentinel has been alerting on `os-cache-seed-e2e-macos-15-x86_64.yml` (#18359, #18373). Investigating #18373 turned up a transient DNS flake on top of a real, long-standing bug: **the macOS 15 x86_64 GWT cache has never once been saved.**

### The bug

`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml` caches `package/osx/build-x86_64/gwt` (restore and save). But `package/osx/make-package:162` only suffixes the arm64 directory:

```sh
BUILD_DIR_X86_64="${PKG_DIR}/build"
BUILD_DIR_ARM64="${PKG_DIR}/build-arm64"
```

x86_64 builds into plain `package/osx/build`. The path looks copied from the arm64 workflow, where `build-arm64` is correct, and has been wrong since the workflow landed in #18324 — #18362 didn't touch it.

Every run of the seed shows the full cycle, even when it succeeds ([run 30313084528](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30313084528)):

- `Cache not found for input keys: rstudio-gwt-x86_64-PRETTY-v2-...`
- GWT compiles into `.../package/osx/build/gwt/bin`
- `Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist` → `Cache save failed.`

### Why it mattered

Because `rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` can never exist on main, the sentinel found it "evicted" on every 2-hourly cycle and dispatched another ~20-minute macOS build that again failed to save it. I confirmed `Evicted from main: rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` → `Dispatching` across four consecutive cycles; there were 12 dispatches on 2026-07-27 alone, on runners that bill at 10x. Repo cache usage sits at 9.79 GiB of the 10 GB quota, so the churn also pressured every other platform's caches. Separately, every macOS 15 x86_64 PR build paid the full GWT compile.

### Changes

1. **Path fix** — point the GWT restore/save at `package/osx/build/gwt`, with a comment recording why x86_64 differs from arm64. No key rotation needed; nothing was ever stored under the `-v2-` key.

2. **Sentinel hardening** (`os-cache-seed-sentinel.yml`) — #18373 was filed for a run that had already been superseded. The dispatch loop runs before the alert check, so the sentinel read a stale conclusion for a seed it had re-dispatched three seconds earlier:
   - Defer the alert while a newer run for that seed is `queued` or `in_progress`.
   - Close the alert issue once the seed's latest completed run succeeds, instead of only suppressing re-alerts while it stays open (both prior alerts needed closing by hand).

### Verification

- Both workflows parse as YAML; the sentinel's `run:` script passes `bash -n`.
- Drove the rewritten alert loop against a mock `gh` across all five branches — recovered-with-open-issue (closes), failure-with-retry-in-flight (defers), failure-with-nothing-in-flight (alerts), failure-with-issue-already-open (skips), and healthy (silent).
- The path fix needs a live seed run on main to confirm the save lands and `rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` appears in main's scope. Worth watching the first post-merge run.

### Note

Auto-closing is a slight behavior change: a genuinely flaky seed will now open and close issues repeatedly rather than holding one open. That seemed better than the current state, where every transient failure leaves manual cleanup, but happy to drop that half if you'd rather the alerts stay sticky.

Addresses #18373

title: stop echoing captured output after any persistent write error
description:
## Summary

An rsession was found spinning at ~93% CPU for hours, flooding its log with `system error 5 (Input/output error)` entries microseconds apart, all from `PosixOutputCapture.cpp:101`. Full diagnosis in #18398; the short version:

- Output capture echoes captured stdout/stderr back to `dup()`'d copies of the original descriptors, so output still reaches the launching terminal.
- When that terminal's pty goes away, the echo `write()` fails with `EIO`. Only `EPIPE`/`EBADF` set the "skip further writes" flag; every other errno was logged on **every** failed write, and retried forever.
- With `log-stderr=1` set (as in the dev config), each logged error is written to fd 2 -- the *redirected* capture pipe -- so the capture thread reads its own error message, fails to echo it, and logs again: a self-sustaining loop at full CPU speed, with continuous log rotation churn on the side. `log-stderr=1` is the sole trigger: the same option both enables the echo writes (it is passed as `forwardOutputToOriginalDescriptors`) and installs the stderr log destination, so the two halves of the loop always arrive together. A stderr logger configured via `logging.conf` alone cannot reproduce this, because without `log-stderr` there are no echo writes to fail.

## Fix

Treat any non-transient write error (anything other than `EAGAIN`/`EINTR`) the way `EPIPE`/`EBADF` were already treated: disable further echo writes and log the error once. The errno-specific message text is folded into a single generic description; the underlying errno is still reported by `systemError`.

Trade-off: a theoretically recoverable errno (say, transient `ENOSPC` on a redirected file) now permanently disables the echo for the remainder of the session, same as a closed pipe always has. Given that the echo target is the launching terminal and the alternative is an unbounded logging loop, that seems like the right side to err on. Client-visible console output is unaffected -- it flows through the capture handlers, not the echo path.

Verified the edited file compiles with the project's real compile flags (`-fsyntax-only` via `compile_commands.json`). Manual verification of the full loop requires killing the launching pty out from under a session with stderr logging enabled.

Addresses #18398.

title: fix session shutdown wedge with an active posit assistant
description:
Addresses #18394.

CI shards have been dying with 300 seconds of output silence (`run-with-heartbeat` exit 124) at session-restart boundaries in the `tests/projects` region. The investigation (see the [issue comment](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/18394#issuecomment-5137219138)) traced it to session shutdowns that never complete when the Posit Assistant chat backend / NES agent are running: the desktop relaunch is driven purely by the rsession child's `exit` event, and the server session proxy only launches a replacement when `connect()` to the session's socket fails -- so an rsession that never finishes `rCleanup()` wedges the whole IDE, silently, in both modes.

Every wait in the shutdown sequence is bounded except one thing: the assistant/chat stop loops pumped the full `module_context::onBackgroundProcessing()` pass (every module's background handlers plus scheduled commands) and `r::session::event_loop::processEvents()` (arbitrary R callbacks) on every poll, mid-teardown. Any blocking item dispatched there wedges the exit permanently, with nothing logged (the whole path was DLOG-only).

Changes:

- **`SessionAssistant.cpp` / `SessionChat.cpp`**: during session shutdown, the stop waits pump only `processSupervisor().poll()` -- which drains the child pipes, flushes the queued shutdown request, and fires the exit callbacks these waits are watching. (Agent I/O handlers already early-return during shutdown, so the full pump delivered nothing else on this path.) If the agent/backend survives SIGTERM plus the grace wait, escalate with SIGKILL to its detached process group -- `terminateProcess()` is a single-pid SIGTERM, `terminateAllChildProcesses()` is off by default in the session, and `exitWithParent` is compiled out on macOS, so a surviving agent was otherwise orphaned forever. The did-not-exit paths now log at WARN so any recurrence localizes itself in the session logs CI already attaches.
- **`session-launcher.ts`** (desktop): `launchNextSession()` now clears `workbenchInitialized` on reload, as the `desktop_launch_session` IPC path already did. Without this, a replacement session dying during startup after a project switch was misread as a crash of a running workbench, the launch error page was suppressed, and the window hung silently on the old dead frame.
- **e2e**: desktop workers now start with `assistant`/`chat_provider` at `"none"` (both default to `"posit"`, so once a @chat suite installed the backend into a worker's data home, every unrelated suite in that worker ran -- and tore down -- the agents on every restart). A per-test fixture guard flips leaked provider prefs back to `"none"` for tests not tagged `@ai`/`@chat`. Desktop-only: server mode shares one config across workers, so a per-test flip there would race concurrently-running @chat suites.
- **e2e**: new `restart-under-agent.test.ts` stress test (@chat lane, desktop-only) that enables the assistant and loops project open/close cycles with the agents live -- the exact workload that wedged CI -- so a recurrence fails visibly in this test instead of killing whatever shard happened to inherit the leaked provider state.

Verification: rsession + core C++ suites pass; desktop typecheck/lint/unit tests pass (one pre-existing environmental failure: `findComponents` needs a built rsession); e2e typecheck passes; the new stress test passes locally against this branch's build. The wedge mechanism is the only unbounded path found in the shutdown sequence, but no stack was ever captured from a wedged CI runner, so the WARN logging is there to confirm or refute recurrence from CI artifacts.

Follow-ups deliberately not in this PR (noted on the issue): the server session proxy has no request deadline; the local-stream acceptor lacks `FD_CLOEXEC` (and the Windows acceptor handle is inheritable), so a non-`ChildProcess` fork can starve session relaunch indefinitely.

title: reduce macos file monitor dropped-event rescan storms
description:
Addresses #18507.

On macOS, heavy filesystem churn in a monitored project (builds, git operations, `npm ci`, ...) can overflow fseventsd's per-client event queue, producing bursts of `File monitor events were dropped; rescanning ...` warnings, each accompanied by a full recursive rescan of the project tree. The bursts are self-amplifying: the recovery rescan runs inline in the FSEvents callback, blocking the run loop long enough for the queue to overflow again.

Three changes:

- **Source-level exclusions.** `file_monitor::registerMonitor` now accepts a best-effort `excludedPaths` hint, applied on macOS via `FSEventStreamSetExclusionPaths` (Linux/Windows ignore it; inotify never watches filtered directories in the first place, and `ReadDirectoryChangesW` has no equivalent). The project monitor passes its always-ignored high-churn directories (`.git`, `.Rproj.user`, `.quarto`, `node_modules`, `renv/library`, `packrat/lib`), so their events are suppressed before they transit the queue rather than being discarded client-side after delivery. Callers must still exclude these paths via the filter; the hint only reduces queue pressure.

- **Debounced recovery rescans.** Dropped-event rescans now run at most once per 10-second interval. Drops arriving inside the interval coalesce into a single deferred trailing rescan, scheduled via a one-shot `CFRunLoopTimer` on the monitor thread's run loop -- the trailing rescan is required for correctness, since dropped changes can postdate what the previous rescan observed. While a deferred rescan is pending, `MustScanSubDirs` recursion in per-path processing is also skipped (fseventsd attaches that flag alongside the drop flags, typically on the root path, so honoring it would perform exactly the scan being deferred). Delivered events continue to be processed normally throughout, so prompt updates are unaffected.

- **Longer stream latency.** The FSEvents latency is raised from 1s to 2s, doubling fseventsd's temporal coalescing window during sustained churn. Streams use `kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer`, so the first event after an idle period is still delivered immediately; only follow-on events batch.

The new `FileMonitorTest.RecursiveExcludedPathSuppressesEvents` test covers the exclusion plumbing end-to-end (and empirically confirms fseventsd excludes events whose path equals the excluded directory, which is the `.git` case under directory-granularity streams). The debounce path requires genuine queue overflow and so is not deterministically unit-testable; verification there is by inspection plus observing warning cadence in real sessions.

All `--scope core` tests pass locally (484 passed, 8 environment-dependent skips).

title: e2e: fix split-editor reload and terminal listing flakes
description:
Fixes the two flaky tests from the [pr-18508 all-platforms e2e run](https://rstudio-playwright-reports.s3.amazonaws.com/pr-18508/31456343700-1/all-platforms/index.html) (5 flaky results total, no hard failures). Neither flake is caused by #18508; both are test-side races.

### `split_editor.test.ts` > the split is restored when the IDE reloads (flaked on all 4 platforms)

The failure trace shows the reload's `client_init` landing ~2s after `open_document`, with no `set_client_state` push in between. The active tab is persisted as the `activeTabDocId` client state value on a passive ~5s timer, so the reload restored a stale value: the failure screenshot shows `split_editor.R` restored but sitting behind `Untitled1`. A background tab is never laid out, so neither its text nor the split (applied on the deferred-layout path) ever renders, and the marker locator matched 0 views for the full 20s budget.

Fix: wait for the `set_client_state` push carrying the active doc id before reloading, exactly as `active_tab_restore.test.ts` already does for #17944. The helper moves to `utils/client-state.ts` so both tests share one implementation.

### `terminal.test.ts` > a file created in the terminal appears in a directory listing (flaked on desktop-macos)

The test required `ztestfile.txt` to appear at least twice in `rstudioapi::terminalBuffer()`: once from the echoed `touch` command and once from the `ls` output. `terminalBuffer()` returns one entry per *physical* line, and the screencast frames show the echoed command wrapping mid-filename (`touch ztest` / `file.txt`) -- the macOS runner's GUID hostname makes the prompt very long, and the terminal pane is narrow. Whether the wrap tears the filename depends on the random sandbox path length, hence the flake.

Fix: type the touch argument with a quote split (`touch "ztest""file.txt"`, the same trick `expectTerminalRenders` already uses), so the echoed command can never contain the contiguous filename. A single intact match is then required, and can only come from the `ls` output, which starts at column 0 and cannot wrap -- so the assertion still proves the file was created and listed.

### Verification

Ran `split_editor.test.ts`, `active_tab_restore.test.ts`, and `terminal.test.ts` locally against a desktop dev build: 16 passed / 0 failed.

title: always capture a stack trace when a test process crashes
description:
## Motivation

On a recent Jenkins `c++-unit-tests` run ([PR-18509 build 2](https://build.posit.it/job/IDE/job/OS-Builds/job/pull-requests/job/open-source-pull-request-build/PR-18509/2/)), the rsession gtest scope segfaulted ~250ms into process startup with no diagnostics whatsoever -- just the shell's `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` line. libSegFault was preloaded, but:

- libSegFault's handler cannot run on an exhausted stack, so stack-overflow segfaults die silently unless the handler is installed on an alternate stack (`SEGFAULT_USE_ALTSTACK`);
- libSegFault was removed from glibc entirely in 2.35+, so newer builders get no crash diagnostics at all (`rstudio-tests` already warns `Could not find libSegFault.so` there).

## Changes

`rstudio-tests.in` (Linux diagnostics; macOS and Windows unchanged):

- set `SEGFAULT_USE_ALTSTACK=1` so libSegFault can report stack-overflow crashes;
- raise the core ulimit for the test process, and on death-by-signal (exit code > 128) locate the fresh core dump and print a `gdb` backtrace from it (capped at 100 frames per thread, since a stack-overflow core otherwise dumps thousands). Handles a relative `core_pattern` (cwd), an absolute one, apport's coredump directory, and systemd-coredump via `coredumpctl`;
- delete examined cores afterwards so reused CI workspaces don't accumulate them.

A timestamp marker ensures only cores produced by the current run are examined.

## Testing

Verified in `ubuntu:20.04` (libSegFault present) and `ubuntu:24.04` (glibc 2.39, no libSegFault) containers, using the rendered harness with null-dereference and stack-overflow crash binaries substituted for the core test suite:

- ubuntu:24.04: both crashes produce a gdb backtrace from the core with correct source frames;
- ubuntu:20.04: both crashes produce a libSegFault backtrace, plus the gdb core backtrace;
- control: the stack-overflow crasher under libSegFault *without* `SEGFAULT_USE_ALTSTACK` reproduces the silent CI failure exactly (only the shell's exit-status line, no backtrace).

Also `bash -n` and `shellcheck` clean.

Developer-only tooling change; no NEWS entry.

title: harden session startup against silent background-thread crashes
description:
## Background

Investigating the silent `c++-unit-tests` segfault on [PR #18509's Jenkins run](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/18509) (rsession died ~250ms into startup, before any test ran, with libSegFault preloaded yet zero output) established the mechanics of *why* such crashes are silent, and turned up several startup hazards that fit the failure signature. Container experiments on the CI image's OS (jammy + glibc-tools libSegFault) confirmed that a fault on a thread with SIGSEGV blocked dies with no handler output whatsoever -- and `safeLaunchThread` / `core::thread::run` block **all** signals on every background thread we start. This is the same family as #10756, which has been observed intermittently for years and never root-caused.

Addresses #10756.

## Changes

1. **`SignalBlocker::blockAll()` no longer blocks synchronous fault signals** (SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGILL, SIGFPE). These are always delivered to the faulting thread, so blocking them cannot route them to the main thread like the async signals this mask exists for -- the kernel simply bypasses any installed crash handler and terminates the process with no diagnostics. Unblocking them costs nothing and makes every background-thread crash reportable.

2. **POSIX `core::system::{getenv,setenv,unsetenv,environment}` are now serialized on a mutex.** glibc's `setenv` can reallocate (and free) the `environ` array while a concurrent `getenv` walks it without locking; the codebase already documents this crash class for the resolver's `LOCALDOMAIN` read (`mainThreadWorkaround()`, rstudio-pro#4628), but the general race remained. The mutex is a plain pthread mutex registered with `pthread_atfork` (lock in prepare, unlock in parent/child) because forked children read the environment before exec (`launchChildProcess` reads `SHELL`), and a fork must not snapshot the mutex in a locked state. Direct `::getenv` callers (libc internals, R) are unaffected either way.

3. **The desktop parent-termination monitor no longer reads the environment on its own thread.** `waitForParentTermination()` read `RS_PPM_FD_READ`/`RS_PPM_FD_WRITE` as the first act of a freshly spawned, fully signal-masked thread, while the main thread's very next statement after spawning it calls `setenv("RS_RPOSTBACK_PATH", ...)` -- a new variable, i.e. the environ-realloc case. This is the best-fitting candidate for the observed crash: it exists only in desktop mode (exactly what `rstudio-tests` runs on the Electron CI flavor via `rdesktop-dev.conf`, and *not* in local server-mode runs), it is silent by mechanism, and it is scheduling-dependent (the CI stage runs in parallel with the GWT unit tests on the same node). The fds are now read on the main thread via a new `parentTerminationFds()` helper and passed into the thread; the no-arg `waitForParentTermination()` remains for compatibility, and the Windows/macOS variants are unchanged.

4. **`initializeLogConfigReload()` now starts at most one SIGHUP reload thread.** Desktop mode initializes logging twice, which previously left two detached threads `sigwait`ing the same SIGHUP and both re-initializing the log on receipt.

## Testing

- New core gtests: `SafeLaunchThreadLeavesFaultSignalsUnblocked` asserts the spawned-thread mask (fault signals unblocked, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP still blocked); `WaitForParentTermination*` cover the fd-based overload's no-parent / normal / abnormal semantics.
- `rstudio-tests --scope core`: 487 tests pass; `--scope rsession`: 416 tests pass (the rsession suite exercises the full startup path -- env locking, new signal masks, parent monitor -- inside a live R session).
- The paired diagnostics change (#18517, merged) means any recurrence of the CI crash now yields a gdb backtrace from the core dump, which will confirm or refute the remaining candidates.

title: fix EnvironmentScope previous-value capture on windows
description:
Fixes the `ide-os-windows/main` build break introduced by #18520 (first red run: build 3710). The new core gtest `EnvironmentTest.EnvironmentScopeRestoresPreviousValue` fails deterministically on Windows:

```
src\cpp\core\system\EnvironmentTests.cpp(79): error: Expected equality of these values:
  "original"
  getenv("RSTUDIO_ENV_SCOPE_TEST")
    Which is: ""
```

### Root cause

`EnvironmentScope` captured the previous value with raw `::getenv`, but `core::system::setenv` writes through `SetEnvironmentVariableW`. On Windows those are two different stores: `::getenv` reads the CRT's `_environ` snapshot taken at process start, which `SetEnvironmentVariable` never updates. Any variable set via `core::system::setenv` was invisible to the scope, so its destructor took the "was unset" path and deleted the variable instead of restoring it. On POSIX both calls hit the same libc `environ`, which is why the test was green locally and on the other platforms.

### Fix

Add an existence-preserving accessor to `core::system`:

```cpp
bool getenv(const std::string& name, std::string* pValue);
```

- POSIX: `::getenv` under the environment lock, `nullptr` -> `false`.
- Windows: `GetEnvironmentVariableW` under the lock (the same store the setters write), with `ERROR_ENVVAR_NOT_FOUND` distinguishing unset.

`EnvironmentScope` now captures the previous value through this overload, keeping the unset vs set-but-empty distinction #18520 introduced (on POSIX; that distinction does not exist on Windows, where setting a variable to the empty string deletes it). This also removes the last raw `::getenv` from the public header, along with the `stdlib.h` and `EnvironmentLock.hpp` includes it needed -- every remaining `EnvironmentLock` user includes that header directly.

The Windows brokenness predates #18520 but never had production impact: the only non-test `EnvironmentScope` user is Apple-only (`SourceIndex.cpp`), and `XdgTests.cpp` is compiled out on Windows, so the new test was the first code to exercise `EnvironmentScope` there.

### Tests

- New gtest `EnvironmentTest.GetenvOverloadDistinguishesUnset` covers unset/set round-trips through `setenv` (which on Windows exercises exactly the CRT-vs-process-block mismatch) plus the POSIX-only set-but-empty case.
- macOS: full core suite green (491 passed / 8 skipped), full backend build clean.
- Windows: not verifiable from this machine -- `Win32Environment.cpp` needs the Windows CI build; the failing test should flip to green on the next `ide-os-windows` run.

title: windows: write environment variables through the CRT as well
description:
On Windows, `core::system::setenv` wrote only the Win32 process environment block, which no C runtime ever re-reads: each CRT keeps its own copy of the environment, initialized lazily from the OS block and updated only by the `putenv` family. Values RStudio set were therefore visible to child processes but invisible to raw `::getenv` readers in-process -- including R itself, whose `Sys.getenv` reads the environment via its C runtime. See #18527 for the full audit and store model.

Changes:

- `core::system::setenv` / `unsetenv` on Windows now also write through our CRT (`_wputenv_s`). This makes post-startup writes (Rtools `PATH` entries, ssh-agent variables) visible to `Sys.getenv` for UCRT builds of R (>= 4.2, which share `ucrtbase.dll` with rsession), makes the pre-startup staging of variables like `RSTUDIO`, `RSTUDIO_CONSOLE_COLOR`, and `R_LIBS_USER` independent of CRT initialization timing, and scrubs read-then-cleared secrets from the CRT copy as well as the OS block. msvcrt builds of R (<= 4.1) still require the existing `r::util::setenv` / `Sys.setenv` bridge; the stale comments there ("R links to a static copy of libc") are updated to describe the actual mechanism.
- The untrusted-directory startup-file suppression set `R_ENVIRON_USER` to the empty string, but Windows deletes a variable assigned an empty value (in every store), so R fell back to processing `~/.Renviron`. On Windows the variable now points at the null device, which parses as an empty Renviron file, silently.
- Tests: a core gtest asserts raw `::getenv` observes `setenv`/`unsetenv` on Windows; an rsession gtest asserts `Sys.getenv` observes a `core::system::setenv` made with R running. 490 core + 417 rsession tests pass locally (macOS); the Windows-specific assertions run in the same suites on Windows CI.

Remaining items from the audit (raw `::getenv("ENV")` migration after #18523, a possible lint for raw CRT environment calls, and manual verification of the untrusted-`.Renviron` behavior on a Windows machine) are tracked on the issue.

Addresses #18527.

title: Split the Sunday E2E rotation and add a certification workflow
description:
## Summary

Two related changes to how the OS E2E engines are scheduled and dispatched.

### Every engine now gets a weekly run

The Sunday cron previously fired all engines at once, and seven Linux configs sat outside the weekday slates entirely, reachable only by hand. Sunday is now three runs, four hours apart, grouped so that every one of the 21 engines is covered exactly once:

| Cron (UTC) | Group | Engines |
|---|---|---|
| `0 8 * * 0` | Linux x86_64 | 9 (8 Desktop plus Ubuntu 24 Server) |
| `0 12 * * 0` | Linux arm64 | 8 |
| `0 16 * * 0` | macOS and Windows, any arch | 4 |

9 + 8 + 4 = 21, with no overlap and no engine left out. Each `ENGINES` entry gained a `platform` field so the selection can group by OS family, which `arch` alone cannot express: macOS and Windows run together regardless of architecture. Each of the three gets its own concurrency group, so an overrun delays only its own next occurrence.

Addresses #18462.

### Certification runs pair each environment with its own R version

Every caller in this repo passed a single hardcoded `r_version` to every engine, so a run-everything dispatch tested one R across all platforms. Certification needs the opposite: specific OS and R combinations.

`os-test-e2e-rstudio-certification.yml` dispatches one engine per cell, each with its own R version, against one RStudio build. The certified pairings live in `.github/e2e-certification/matrix.json` so the scope is a reviewable file rather than a value buried in workflow YAML. These 13 cells are what a plain dispatch runs:

| Environment | Arch | R | | Environment | Arch | R |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu 22.04 | x86_64 | 4.3.3 | | Ubuntu 24.04 Server | x86_64 | 4.4.1 |
| Ubuntu 24.04 | x86_64 | 4.4.1 | | macOS 14 | arm64 | 4.1.3 |
| Ubuntu 26.04 | arm64 | 4.6.1 | | macOS 15 | x86_64 | 4.4.3 |
| Debian 13 | arm64 | 4.2.3 | | macOS 26 | arm64 | 4.5.1 |
| Fedora 43 | x86_64 | distro | | Windows Server 2025 | x86_64 | 4.6.1 |
| Fedora 44 | arm64 | distro | | | | |
| Rocky 9 | x86_64 | 4.4.3 | | | | |
| Rocky 10 | arm64 | 4.6.1 | | | | |

Each Linux distro is certified on one architecture, split four and four with arm64 on the newer releases. The file also carries the other architecture of each distro, so those eight cells can be selected by name without being run by default. Every R version was checked as actually installable on its assigned architecture before being committed.

Two optional inputs override the file -- `cells` for which environments run, and `r_overrides` for `cell=version` pairs. They are separate so bumping one environment's R version does not mean retyping the whole set. Both validate every name and fail before provisioning a runner.

Version pinning and build-from-source both work: the installer-URL resolution now composes with the branch's own daily manifest (`os-resolve-daily-manifest`), so a pinned run always installs a build from the same release line as the tests it runs. RStudio ships one Debian package per Ubuntu-family line and one RPM per RHEL-family line rather than one per release, so several cells install the same binary and differ only in the OS under test; the summary table notes which, computed from the URLs actually resolved.

Addresses #18463.

### Reporting which R actually ran

The four Fedora engines set `r_install: "distro"`, install R from the distro's own repos, and ignore `r_version` entirely -- silently, so nothing recorded which R a run really used. The certification summary now reports the version read back from the installed R rather than echoed from the request, so a Fedora cell shows the concrete version dnf supplied and an ignored pin cannot hide:

| Environment | R requested | R actually used | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rocky9-x86_64` | 4.4.3 | 4.4.3 | success |
| `fedora44-arm64` | distro | 4.6.1 | success |

Non-Linux engines return it as a `workflow_call` output. The Linux Desktop cells run as one matrix call whose outputs collapse to a single value, so each uploads its version and its own result as an artifact instead -- which is also what stops one failing Linux cell from being reported against every other cell in the matrix. The R version also lands on every E2E job's summary page, for all callers rather than just certification.

### Supporting changes

- The installer-URL resolution moved to `.github/actions/os-resolve-daily-urls`, composing with upstream's `os-resolve-daily-manifest` so both this workflow and the scheduled rotation resolve a build from the branch's own release line rather than the `/rstudio/latest` alias.
- Fixed two `os-e2e-deps` package-install failures found by a real certification run: a recommended package (`MASS`) was being reinstalled from CRAN despite shipping with R, which the current CRAN release cannot satisfy below R 4.4.0; and `pak` was installed from a repo lacking a binary for some platform/R combinations, now installed from its own repository instead.
- `.github/e2e-linux/README.md` gained an R-versions section: `r_install` decides whether `r_version` is honored, and `os-e2e-deps` keys its caches on the resolved R major.minor.

## Verification

- A full 13-cell, full-suite certification run pinned to a real release-branch build, run twice (before and after the package-install fixes above). Confirmed `rig add <version>` followed by a matching installed version on every cell, both container engines (Fedora, Rocky) completing cleanly for the first time, and the summary table correctly attributing per-cell results so one failing cell never gets reported against its siblings.
- A bash harness replays the real `pick` and `summary` scripts across 64 assertions: selection, sparse overrides, both separator styles, the `distro` sentinel, selecting a non-default cell by name, every fatal-error path, a missing artifact degrading rather than breaking the table, a summary-fetch failure reported distinctly from a cell that never ran, and the shared-binary grouping.
- The three Sunday selections were replayed against the live `ENGINES` array, asserting sizes 9/8/4, zero pairwise overlap, and a union equal to all 21.
- `actionlint` clean, with no new warnings against base.

title: Wire e2e engines to retrieve Posit AI credentials from 1Password
description:
## Summary
- Wire the remaining 5 e2e engines (macOS 15, macOS 26, macOS 14, Windows, Ubuntu server) to retrieve Posit AI test credentials from 1Password via `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`, matching the existing Linux desktop implementation.
- Add `environment: e2e-playwright` to all 6 engine jobs so the environment-scoped secret takes precedence over the repo-level one.
- Forward `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` from the real PR and scheduled callers (`os-test-e2e-rstudio-pr.yml` and the scheduled workflows), since the environment override only takes effect once the secret name reaches the called job.
- Pin the Linux e2e workflow and its shared composite actions to commit SHAs.
- Add a temporary CODEOWNERS entry for `e2e/rstudio/.env.op` pending a real reviewing team.

Validated with a temporary trigger workflow across all 6 platforms (real Posit AI sign-in confirmed via `open-chat-pane.test.ts`), then removed before merge.

title: fix breakpoints in S7 methods for S7 generics
description:
Fixes #18531.

## Problem

Breakpoints set inside methods registered on S7 generics (`S7::new_generic()`) never fire, on any R version. The gutter shows a normal breakpoint marker, but execution runs straight through it with no error or warning. This is the sibling of #18526, which covered S7 methods for *S3* generics; this dispatch path was wired up by the same #16490 work but its test only covered the S3-generic case.

## Root cause

`.rs.setBreakpointImpl` correctly locates the method in the generic's methods environment, but the `trace()` call inside `.rs.setFunctionBreakpoints` fails: the stored method has class `c("S7_method", "function", "S7_object")`, and the methods package cannot derive a trace class from a length-3 class vector:

```
Error in !is.null(prototype) && is.na(match(name, .BasicClasses)) :
  'length = 3' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
```

The error is swallowed by the `tryCatch` in `.rs.setBreakpoint`, so the breakpoint is silently dropped.

## Fix

Strip the class from the stored method before tracing (stashing it in an attribute on the function), so the standard `functionWithTrace` machinery applies, and restore the class when breakpoints are cleared and `untrace()` has put the stripped copy back. S7 dispatch calls whatever function is stored in the methods environment, so the traced method works normally while breakpoints are active, and the method round-trips back to its original state (class, body, and attributes) when they are cleared.

## Verification

- New e2e test `'breakpoints fire in S7 methods for S7 generics (#18531)'`, red/green verified locally against a dev session: fails without the R change (same `waitForDebugMode` timeout signature as the #16490 test's certification failures), passes with it. The existing S3-generic test still passes.
- A scoping harness driving the real `SessionBreakpoints.R` through the full lifecycle (resolve steps -> set -> fire on dispatch -> re-resolve steps while traced -> clear -> class/attribute restore -> normal dispatch) passes on R 4.6.1.
- On R < 4.3.0 this path additionally needs #18530's property-access fix; the harness confirms the two changes compose (all lifecycle checks pass on R 4.2.3 with both applied). The branches touch adjacent but non-overlapping code, so they can merge in either order.

title: fix rserver double session launch that leaks an orphaned rsession
description:
Fixes #18572. Fixes #18571.

An R session restart on RStudio Server could leak an orphaned rsession that runs forever. Root-caused from the rserver debug log of [e2e run 31839732347](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/31839732347/job/94897988955): after the old session acked `suspend_for_restart` and exited, rserver launched **two** replacements one second apart. An RPC still in flight to the exiting session died with EOF, and `handleRpcError` unconditionally removed the pending-launch record of the first replacement (spawned 37 ms earlier); the retrying `/rpc/ping`'s one-second launch throttle then spawned a second one. Both booted, the second re-bound the session stream socket, and the first became unreachable -- never contacted, never told to exit, holding the project source-database lock (surfacing the "previous R session terminated abnormally" dialog) and the Posit Assistant install lock, and reacting to shared user-prefs changes indefinitely.

Two fixes:

- **`ServerSessionManager::removePendingLaunch`** no longer erases a pending launch on the request-error paths while the launched process is still alive: a request failing for the context says nothing about the health of a separately launched, still-booting session. The existing safety nets still clear the entry -- the SIGCHLD process tracker (#18208) when the pid dies, and `launchSession`'s one-minute window otherwise. Custom session launchers never record a pid and keep the old clear-on-error behavior. (Also moves `core::system::isProcessRunning` out of the Linux-only branch of `PosixSystem.cpp`; it is plain POSIX, was declared unconditionally in the header, and failed to link on macOS.)
- **The Posit Assistant install lock owner id** is now unique per process (`<session-id>-<uuid>`). It was the bare session id, which is stable across relaunches, so an orphaned predecessor held a live lock under its replacement's own name and every `chat_start_backend` in the replacement failed with a spurious, never-clearing "A Posit Assistant update is in progress." With the per-process id, even an orphan can only make mutations (update/uninstall) refuse -- correctly, since the install genuinely is in use -- while backend starts coexist, which is the supported multi-session steady state.

Follow-ups noted on #18572 and deliberately not included: the success path (`handleProxyResponse`) has a much narrower variant of the same race, and an rsession could self-detect a supplanted stream socket and exit.

Verification:

- New tests: `SessionManagerTest.RequestErrorKeepsPendingLaunchOfLiveProcess`, `RequestErrorClearsPendingLaunchOfDeadProcess`, `RequestErrorClearsPendingLaunchWithoutRecordedPid`; `ChatInstallLock.SameOwnerIdCollidesWithLivePredecessor`.
- `rstudio-tests --scope rsession`: 418/418 pass. `--scope rserver`: all `SessionManagerTest` and proxy tests pass (the `SqliteDBActiveSessionStorageTest` failures are environmental on this machine and identical on main's build).

title: fix chat guardrails blocking package installs under a restrictive umask
description:
## Summary

Posit Assistant's `install.packages()` fails in Workbench sessions running under a restrictive umask (common in hardened containers), with repeated "One or more agent file operations were blocked" errors that eventually push the model to work around the sandbox via `Rscript` in the terminal.

Root cause: the guardrails' world-readable check in `.rs.chat.isFileReadAllowed()` denied reads of any file lacking the o+r permission bit, unconditionally. Under umask 077 every file the session creates is mode 600, so agent code was blocked from reading files R itself had just written. The most visible victim is the `installed.packages()` cache (`tempdir()/libloc_*.rds`): the cache gets seeded by the IDE or an earlier command, and the next read -- during `install.packages()` dependency resolution -- hits the hooked `readRDS()` and errors. The same check also blocked the agent from reading *any* user-owned file (project files included) in such environments. The `chat.safeFunctions` trusted-caller allowlist did not help, because trust only bypasses the deny-path patterns, not the permission check.

## Changes

- **Scope the world-readable check to paths outside the allowed roots** (tempdir, working directory, project directory, scratch path, `.libPaths()`, R user dirs). These are locations the agent may already *write* to, so denying reads there was incoherent -- and they are exactly where the session's own non-world-readable files live. The allowed roots are now enumerated in one place (`chat.allowedRoots()`), shared by the edit check and the read check.
- **Neutralize the check when the umask itself strips world-read from new files.** On a default-umask system a 600-mode file is a deliberate signal (ssh keys, tokens) and the heuristic has value; under umask 077 every file is private by default, the bit carries no signal, and the heuristic just denied everything.
- **Allow edits within a not-yet-created user library** (`R_LIBS_USER`), so `install.packages()` can create the personal library on first use (a nonexistent user library is not in `.libPaths()`, so it was previously denied).

The deny-path patterns (credentials, `.env`, `.Renviron`, `~/.ssh`, system files) still apply everywhere, including within the allowed roots and regardless of umask.

## Security trade-offs

These guardrails target accidental misuse, not malicious code (per the note at the top of `SessionChat.R`). Two deliberate loosenings here:

1. A non-world-readable file *inside* the project/tempdir/library roots is now readable by agent code. Deny patterns still catch the common credential shapes there. The home directory itself is never a read-exempt root (it is the fallback working directory when no project is open), and the `.ssh` read-deny pattern covers all non-public files.
2. On umask-restricted systems, a private file outside the allowed roots that matches no deny pattern is now readable.
